The east watch tower buckles inward without impact.
The ground under the ration post drops three inches.
The table slides across the stone by itself.

Everyone wakes into motion.

HARJEEV:
East side!
Move!
Move!

No chaos.
Only speed.

Addy to roof angle.
Knight to center command.
Raevan and Chug to brace line.
Yassine and Kaizen to moving supports.
Sorya to the pressure seam.

The crush line pushes like invisible tide.

CHUG:
Where is he?!

KNIGHT:
Doesn't matter!
Break the anchor source!

Sorya closes her eyes and feels the pressure trail.

SORYA:
South ridge!
Buried sigil!

Yassine runs first.
Too fast to ask.
Good.

Chug follows.
Better.

They crest the ridge and find it:
a black stone plate driven into the earth with Eleven's mark burning on it.

Six chained weights circle it, sinking deeper every second.

YASSINE:
Kill the plate?

CHUG:
Kill the weights first!

They move together.

Blade.
Bolt.
Cord.
Stone.
Again.

The pull weakens.

Back in camp the table stops sliding.

Harjeev later calls that the second time the table saved morale by existing.

He is probably right.

[SCENE 8 — VARKUL SEEN]

As the last weight snaps, something huge moves on the far cliff opposite them.

Not close.

Not reachable.

Just visible enough.

A silhouette like a fortress learning to walk.

Broad shoulders.
Heavy chain mantle.
Hammer head over one shoulder so large it changes the horizon line around it.

Varkul.

No.11.

He does not come down.
He only watches the two of them break his anchor plate.

Then he nods once.

Like a mason checking foundation work.

VARKUL:
Better than debris.
Not yet structure.

Yassine bares a blade toward the cliff.

YASSINE:
Come down then!

VARKUL:
No.
Not until your walls begin to believe in themselves.

He turns.
The whole ridge seems to lean with him.

Then he is gone.

[SCENE 9 — CHUG HATES THIS FIGHT]

Back at camp, Chug kicks the broken anchor plate across the yard.

CHUG:
I hate him.

KNIGHT:
Good.

CHUG:
Don't say good.

KNIGHT:
Why?
You should hate him.
He is forcing you to win without getting the satisfaction of direct violence.

CHUG:
Exactly.

KNIGHT:
Then learn from the discomfort.

Chug almost throws the frame.

Doesn't.

Growth again.
Annoying growth.

RAEVAN:
He wants you emotional because emotion is easier to pull than stone.

KAIZEN:
And easier to stampede.

HARJEEV:
Also harder to ration.

YASSINE:
He really can make logistics sound spiritual.

HARJEEV:
You're welcome.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 28]

That night Knight redraws the whole camp route grid.

Twice.

Then once more.

Addy shifts to rotating high-angle watch.
Yassine gets two patrol lanes and one interior response lane.
Chug is assigned central breaker and anchor destruction.
Not front champion.

He stares at the board.

CHUG:
I still don't like that.

KNIGHT:
I know.
That's why it's right.

Guide speaks from the rafters somewhere above the fire.

GUIDE:
Eleven is teaching the camp whether it is a shelter or a system.

Chug looks at the walls.
The table.
The marked sectors.
The people already moving inside structure instead of against it.

CHUG:
Then we answer him.

System text burns dim and cold in the night.

SYSTEM:
"DRAKO 11 PRESSURE ACTIVE"
"CAMP ROLE INTEGRATION: IMPROVED"

[BOSS GATE — Nexter No.6 Kaith]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for VARKUL'S WEATHER.

29.text:
[SCENE 1 — THE DAY OF STRUCTURE]

Varkul comes at dawn.

This time with his body.

No hidden plate.
No weather crew first.
No voice in the stone.

He simply appears at the south ridge and starts walking.

The camp feels him before the watchers call him.

Every nail hums.
Every bowl trembles.
Every weak joint confesses itself.

Knight is standing before the call fully finishes.

KNIGHT:
Positions!

Harjeev doesn't shout.
He assigns.

HARJEEV:
Med left!
Ration clear!
Roof line Addy!
North brace Yassine!
Center breaker Chug!
No one freelances!

No one does.

That matters more than heroics would.

Varkul reaches the perimeter line and stops outside it.

He is bigger than Arowh.
Not broader in pure muscle.
Heavier in intent.

His armor is built of linked dark plates and chain-weight discs that hang like broken moons.
The hammer rests against one shoulder, head as tall as Addy's torso.

VARKUL:
So this is the camp that made Twelve kneel.

CHUG:
You came far to lose.

VARKUL:
No.
I came because I heard your walls speaking before your men did.

That line goes under Chug's skin instantly.

Good.
Now he knows what the fight is again.

[SCENE 2 — FIRST IMPACT]

Varkul doesn't rush.

He plants the hammer once.

The entire south line sinks.

Not breaks.
Sinks.

One brace cracks.
One post folds.
A whole warning circle tears out of alignment.

SORYA:
There!

Addy fires before the order finishes.
Arrow into the chain-disc cluster on Varkul's left side.
It clangs.
Distracts.
Not enough.

Raevan drives the spear into the ground where the pressure wave should continue and splits the path.

YASSINE:
Move!

Chug is already moving.

Not at Varkul's chest.

At the anchor chain hanging behind his right knee.

Frame-bolt.

The chain snaps free from one ring.

Varkul actually turns his head.

VARKUL:
Good.
You finally learned where weight lives.

CHUG:
Shut up and fall.

VARKUL:
Not yet.

[SCENE 3 — CAMP FIGHT, NOT DUEL]

This fight is ugly.

Not cinematic.
Not glorious.

Varkul hits sectors, not people.

He smashes support lines.
Collapses ladders.
Drives pressure through the ground toward supply zones.

He is trying to prove Knight right.

Trying to show that Chug is still only good at direct opposition.

So Chug stops giving him that.

He moves between roles instead.

Center to south brace.
South brace to ration lane.
Ration lane to Addy's fallback.

Every time Varkul creates a break, Chug fills the gap long enough for someone else to fix it.

Knight notices first.

KNIGHT:
There.
Keep that.

Addy fires over his shoulder.

ADDY:
Left! Left!

Chug ducks.
Arrow passes over him and buries into the hammer grip seam.

Varkul's next swing shifts half an inch off line.

Enough for Yassine to cross under and cut one of the weight discs free.

HARJEEV:
Write that one down too!

Even in crisis he is still a energyger.
Maybe that is why the camp survives.

[SCENE 4 — THE HAMMER LESSON]

Varkul tires of playing with the perimeter.

He steps through it.

Now he is inside the camp.

That changes everything.

The walls do not matter anymore.
Only the structure inside people's heads.

Varkul swings the hammer in a low arc.
Not for kills.
For displacement.

The table shudders.
The med post nearly flips.
One whole section of marked floor gets erased.

CHUG sees it and finally understands:
Eleven is trying to delete organization faster than the camp can remember it.

GUIDE:
Now.

Chug hears the answer before he thinks it.

CHUG:
Table first! Hold the table!

It sounds ridiculous.
Until everyone moves on it instantly.

Yassine to left support.
Harjeev and Addy clearing the med line.
Knight and Raevan on Varkul's weapon side.
Sorya restoring one pressure mark under the table legs.
Kaizen driving two panicked fighters back into lanes with nothing but voice.

For one second the whole camp moves as one body.

Varkul sees it.

VARKUL:
...There.

Not praise.

Recognition again.

He hates that he keeps getting it from enemies.

Maybe that's why it matters.

[SCENE 5 — ADDY FULLY ARRIVES]

A collapse wave knocks Addy from the roofline.

Not far.
Far enough.

She lands badly and rolls, bow nearly lost.

The old control residue flashes across her face for a split second.

Wrong eyes.
Wrong stillness.

Chug sees it.
So does she.

ADDY:
No.

She forces the bow back up with both hands.
Breathes once.
Twice.

Then fires four arrows in under three seconds.

One takes a chain ring.
One takes a hammer seam.
One takes the edge of Varkul's jaw guard.
The fourth pins a falling supply beam before it crushes Harjeev.

Harjeev looks at the beam.
Then at her.

HARJEEV:
Fine.
Write all of those down.

Addy actually laughs.

Short.
Sharp.
Alive.

That laugh means she is back enough to matter.

[SCENE 6 — VARKUL BREAKS THE GROUND]

Enraged or impressed—
with Drakos it is hard to tell—

Varkul slams both hands onto the hammer shaft and drives it deep.

The whole camp floor lurches.

Not metaphor.
Actual lurch.

The center line splits.

The table tilts.

One leg breaks.

Yassine grabs the edge first.
Chug catches the other side.
Knight plants his blade under the slab and holds.
Harjeev keeps the ledgers from scattering.
Sorya seals the crack with a pressure line so thin it almost breaks her nose in blood.

VARKUL:
Good.
Now choose:
camp...
or kill.

That is the question.

That is always what Eleven wanted.

Chug breathes.
Looks at the table.
Looks at the camp.
Looks at Varkul.

Then answers correctly.

CHUG:
Both.

Knight's eyes flick toward him.
Fast.
Approving.
Gone.

[SCENE 7 — THE PLAN IN MOTION]

Knight starts barking orders with machine precision.

KNIGHT:
Addy, left eye line!
Yassine, rear chains!
Raevan, ground denial!
Sorya, narrow seam under hammer base!
Harjeev, clear the center lane!
Chug—finish the anchor!

This is leadership multiplied.
Not one man.
A chain.

Good.

Varkul swings again.
Too late.

Addy's arrow drives into the slit below his left eye guard.
Not deep.
Distracting.

Yassine cuts two rear weight chains.
Raevan's spear pins one boot line in place.
Sorya's seam thins the ground under the hammer head.
Harjeev clears the exact space Chug needs to move through.

Chug opens Rage 1.

Clean.

No waste.
No blind fury.

Just sharpened acceleration.

He uses the broken table leg as a stepping point,
vaults higher than Varkul expects,
lands on the hammer shaft,
runs its length,
and drives the frame-bolt straight into the exposed central chain lock at Varkul's chest.

The lock explodes.

All the hanging weight discs drop at once.

Varkul staggers under his own redistributed load.

For the first time,
the camp is heavier for him than for them.

[SCENE 8 — DRAKO NO.11 FALLS]

Yassine's blades cross the hamstring seam.
Knight cuts the throat guard tie.
Raevan slams the spear butt into the wounded knee.

Varkul falls.

Not to one knee like Arowh.

Flat.

One hand still on the hammer.
One shoulder buried in dust.
Armor discs spread around him like a collapsed orbit.

The whole camp goes silent.

Even the wounded stop groaning for a second.

Chug stands over him.
Breathing hard.
Rage dropping cleanly.
No panic.
No shaking.

Varkul looks up through blood and dust.

VARKUL:
...Structure.

CHUG:
Yeah.

VARKUL:
So Twelve was right.

CHUG:
About what?

VARKUL:
You stopped trying to become the whole wall.

That line lands deeper than the victory does.

Because it is the exact lesson Knight kept beating into him.
Because hearing it from a defeated Drako makes it undeniable.

VARKUL plants one hand under himself, trying to rise.

Knight puts a blade to the throat gap.
Not trembling.

VARKUL looks at him and snorts blood.

VARKUL:
Do it then.

Knight doesn't.

He looks at Chug instead.

Choice again.

Chug hates how often growth requires choosing mercy under witnesses.

Then again, maybe that is the point.

CHUG:
Walk.
And tell Ten the camp stays standing.

Varkul studies him for one long second.

Then laughs once.
Low.
Cracked.
Not amused.
Just grimly informed.

VARKUL:
He will come for the names, not the walls.

That sentence freezes everyone harder than the fight did.

Then Varkul tears his own route mark free from the armor chain and drops it at Chug's boots.

VARKUL:
Eleven falls.
Remember what that cost you.

He leaves dragging the hammer, too wounded to carry it cleanly.

Still walking.

Still defeated.

Still dangerous enough that no one relaxes until the pressure in the ground fully lifts.

[SCENE 9 — WHAT IT COST]

The camp survived.

Not untouched.

One watch line broken.
One wall gone.
Three wounded hard.
One table leg shattered.
Half the med cloth used.
One bowstring snapped.
Two route markers lost.
Addy's hands trembling from the residue spike.
Yassine's shoulder reopened.
Chug's ribs screaming under the bandage.

Harjeev writes every cost down before anyone can romanticize the win.

HARJEEV:
Good.
Now the victory is real.

ADDY:
You really need a different religion.

HARJEEV:
No.
This one keeps inventory.

Knight lifts the broken table leg Chug used to launch.

KNIGHT:
Keep this.

Chug takes it.

CHUG:
Why?

KNIGHT:
Because one day you'll forget it wasn't your power that won today.
It was everyone else's shape around it.

That line goes under the skin and stays there.

Good.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 29]

At night Harjeev opens the ledger again.

DRAKO NO.11 — VARKUL
DEFEATED

The room around the fire changes when he writes it.

Not celebration.
Certainty.

Two down.

Not myth anymore.
Method.

Addy binds a new string with steady hands.
Yassine sleeps sitting up by the table because exhaustion beat pride.
Raevan repairs sectors.
Sorya redraws lines.
Kaizen finally lets Chug rest.
Knight marks a new empty route on the board.

Harjeev notices.

HARJEEV:
Ten?

KNIGHT:
Soon.

Chug looks at the two route marks nailed beneath the table now.

TWELVE.
ELEVEN.

He feels no thrill.

Only momentum.

Guide speaks once into the dark rafters.

GUIDE:
Now the war knows your camp by shape, not rumor.

Chug closes his eyes once.

CHUG:
Good.

Then opens them.

CHUG:
Let it learn the rest.

System text burns like iron.

SYSTEM:
"DRAKO 11 STATUS: DOWN"
"CAMP STATUS: HELD UNDER COLLAPSE"
"NEXT THREAT VECTOR OPENING"
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — BREAKING ELEVEN]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

30.text: PART 30 — THE NAME IN THE MED LEDGER

[SCENE 1 — TWO MARKS UNDER THE TABLE]

Morning settles differently after Eleven falls.

The camp does not look stronger.

It looks used.

Which is better.

Under the map table two route marks hang now:
Twelve.
Eleven.

The empty seat beside Tora's ring remains empty.
Not symbolic anymore.
Prepared.

Harjeev calls the morning report without ceremony.

HARJEEV:
Cloth low.
Water fair.
Arrow stock down.
South wall repair needed.
North watch stable.
Three fighters active.
Two limited.
One recovering from pretending she's indestructible.

ADDY:
I was indestructible enough.

HARJEEV:
No.
You were expensive.

Yassine snorts into his cup.

Knight points at the board.

KNIGHT:
We do not chase Ten blind.

CHUG:
Who said blind?

KNIGHT:
You implied sprinting twice before breakfast.

That is unfortunately true.

Chug lets it go.

Growth again.
Annoying growth again.

[SCENE 2 — THE SECOND RELAY STONE]

Harjeev brings out the last black journal.

The one he had not opened yet.

Thinner.
Cracked.
Burned at the edge.

HARJEEV:
Found deeper than the first relay.
Thought it was slag.
It wasn't.

He opens it carefully.

The stone leaves scrape.

More names.
Less clean.

Some are gone entirely.
Some reduced to initials and route tags.

SOLO — MOVING
NEONKD — UNKNOWN
REE — HELD
FRIEND — ROUTE CUT
L.O.O. — UNREADABLE
A.D. — RECOVERED? FALSE?
M.R. — MED / TRANSFER / UNSTABLE

The whole table goes still.

Chug reads that line again.

M.R.

No title.
No context.
Just name, med, transfer, unstable.

Yassine frowns.

YASSINE:
Do we know that one?

Chug doesn't answer immediately.

Because the name does something strange.
Not memory exactly.
Pressure.
An old rank.
A place at the top of a circle.

CHUG:
...Yeah.

ADDY:
How yeah?

CHUG:
High.
Close.
Top of the old friend ranks.

Knight looks at him carefully.

KNIGHT:
Name.

CHUG:
M.R.

HARJEEV taps the line.

HARJEEV:
Medical transfer.
Unstable.
Moved, not dead.

SORYA:
Injury?

HARJEEV:
Not specified.
Only route markings and one broken med code.

Addy leans closer.

ADDY:
Which code?

Harjeev traces the mark.

HARJEEV:
Multiple wound stabilization.
Chest or side trauma.
Possibly internal.
Possibly mobility-compromised at time of movement.

Yassine sits back slowly.

YASSINE:
So someone's carrying him.
Or dragging him.

CHUG's jaw tightens.

CHUG:
Then we find him too.

Knight does not shut it down.
That matters.

[SCENE 3 — M.R., SPOKEN OUT LOUD]

The camp has new weight now.

Not a visible threat.
A name.

Chug walks to the outer stones after the report and says it once under his breath.

CHUG:
M.R.

Guide speaks before the echo dies.

GUIDE:
You remember the rank before the face.

CHUG:
Yeah.

GUIDE:
That should concern you.

CHUG:
Everything concerns me.

GUIDE:
No.
This one specifically.

Chug turns toward the empty air.

CHUG:
Why?

Long pause.

GUIDE:
Because some names come back before they should.

That answer is useless.
And not.
Which is Guide's favorite kind.

Chug hates it.

Good.
Hatred keeps the line awake.

[SCENE 4 — CAMP REPAIR IS STORY TOO]

For the next stretch, the camp builds.

Not glamorous.
Important.

South wall replaced with layered stone and chain support.
Addy's high post rebuilt with shield slats.
Med line moved farther from the main crush axis.
New table leg carved from basin timber brought back from Varkul's field.

Yassine helps Harjeev set brace pins.

Badly at first.

HARJEEV:
No.
If you hammer like that, the pin remembers insult and leaves later.

YASSINE:
That's not how metal works.

HARJEEV:
It is in camps.

ADDY, from the roof:
Manager magic.

HARJEEV:
Management is magic for people who survive paperwork.

Knight and Raevan argue over lane spacing.
Sorya argues with both and wins.
Kaizen pretends not to help and somehow improves everything anyway.

Chug spends more time carrying, bracing, and fixing than fighting.

At first it frustrates him.

Then he realizes:
this is also training.

Holding.
Not just hitting.

Camp work is structure made visible.

That is why Tora cared.
That is why Varkul attacked it.
That is why M.R. being in a med ledger feels worse than a name on a kill board.

Because if he comes back wrong,
there needs to be something here able to hold him without breaking.

[SCENE 5 — ADDY'S FULL STATUS]

Near evening Addy joins the route drill with no restriction marker.

Knight erases her recovery note and replaces it with active rotation.

ADDY:
So that's it?
No ceremony?

HARJEEV:
You want a parade?
We're short on flags.

YASSINE:
And joy.

ADDY:
Fair.

Raevan hands her a heavier bow.

ADDY:
That's not mine.

RAEVAN:
It is now.
Draw.

She does.

The heavier frame shivers once.
Then obeys.

RAEVAN:
Good.
You're back enough to matter.

Addy lowers the bow and glances away before anyone can make it emotional.

CHUG:
Good to have you active.

ADDY:
You say that like I wasn't already useful.

CHUG:
You know what I mean.

ADDY:
Yeah.

Beat.

ADDY:
I know.

[SCENE 6 — A NAME THAT CHANGES CHUG]

That night, Yassine catches Chug staring at the M.R. line in the relay stone again.

YASSINE:
You really knew him.

CHUG:
Yeah.

YASSINE:
Higher than Tora?

Chug takes a while.

CHUG:
Different.
Tora was force.
M.R. was...
top rank for a reason.

YASSINE:
Meaning?

CHUG:
He could walk into a room and make people reorganize around him without trying.
Fast.
Sharp.
Reliable.
Too reliable maybe.

YASSINE:
You trust him?

Chug doesn't answer immediately.

That is answer enough.

YASSINE:
Huh.

CHUG:
What?

YASSINE:
Just trying to imagine someone you trusted that much.

Chug almost says something easy.

Doesn't.

CHUG:
Yeah.
Me too.

That honesty costs him something.
Which means it was the right version.

[SCENE 7 — THE RUMOR OF TEN]

Late watch.

The west wind changes.

Sorya stands at the perimeter and listens to the air itself.

SORYA:
Ten is moving.

KNIGHT:
How do you know?

SORYA:
Morale pressure.
Not gravity.
Not route collapse.
Something lower and wider.
Like dread looking for language.

Knight marks a line on the board.

KNIGHT:
Ten burns confidence.
If he comes straight, camp morale breaks before walls do.

HARJEEV:
Then we fix what can be fixed before he smells weakness.

ADDY:
Comforting sentence.

HARJEEV:
Accurate sentence.

Guide speaks low.

GUIDE:
Ten will not respect stone.
He will respect fractures in people.

Chug looks around the camp.
At Addy's hands.
At Yassine's half-memory.
At the empty seat.
At the new name in the ledger.

M.R.

Unstable.

Moved.

Still somewhere inside this war.

The pressure of that name does not weaken him.

It sharpens him.

Good.
That is what matters.

[SCENE 8 — THE FIRST MENTION TO THE WHOLE CAMP]

Harjeev closes the relay journal and says it out loud so everyone hears it equally.

HARJEEV:
There is one more name on the board now.
M.R.
Alive enough to transfer.
Injured enough to note.
Unstable enough to matter.

The camp absorbs it.

Addy repeats it once.

ADDY:
M.R.

Yassine too.

YASSINE:
M.R.

Knight says nothing.

But he writes the initials on the board beside SOLO and REE.

Three rescue vectors now.

Three future wounds.

Three reasons the camp cannot afford to stay small.

CHUG looks at the board.

Not at the enemies.
At the names.

He understands something then.

Drakos and Nexters are not the whole war.

The whole war is what survives after you bring people back.

That is the bigger thing.
The harder thing.

He almost says it aloud.

Doesn't.

It is not ready for words yet.

[SCENE 9 — END OF 30]

Before sleep, Chug places a new mark on the table himself.

Not a trophy.

Not a route tag.

A simple carved line beside the empty seat.

M.R.

No explanation.
No announcement.

Just a place prepared before the person arrives.

Guide's voice comes softer than usual.

GUIDE:
Careful what seats you prepare.
Some men return changed enough to deserve none.

Chug doesn't look up.

CHUG:
Then we'll decide that when he gets here.

GUIDE:
Will you?

Chug's hand rests once on the carved initials.

M.R.

Injured somewhere.
Moved somewhere.
Still inside the game.

CHUG:
Yeah.
We will.

The fire lowers.
The camp breathes.
The board holds.

And somewhere beyond route lines and broken sectors and Drako marks,
a man named M.R. survives badly enough to still be written down.

System text burns low across the table edge.

SYSTEM:
"ALLY ADDY — FULL PLAYABLE STATUS CONFIRMED"
"NEW NAME ADDED: M.R."
"NEXT DRACO VECTOR: TEN"
"CAMP STRUCTURE LEVEL: REINFORCED"

[BOSS GATE — Drako No.8 Kade]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for THE NAME IN THE MED LEDGER.

31.text: PART 31 — THE ROAD THAT CUTS BACK

[SCENE 1 — AFTER ELEVEN]

Camp does not celebrate after Varkul.

It reorganizes.

That is worse for enemies and better for everyone else.

Harjeev adds a second ledger page just for repairs.

Knight redraws the patrol arcs.

Raevan doubles the moving-range drills.

Sorya marks three more field warning lines near the east stones.

Kaizen says less than usual, which means he is thinking something unpleasant.

Chug stands at the map table looking at the names.

SOLO.

NEONKD.

REE.

FRIEND.

M.R.

And the old carved mark where he wrote M.R. by hand.

The camp is larger now, but the board is still missing too many people.

YASSINE:

You're doing that thing again.

CHUG:

What thing?

YASSINE:

Staring like the table owes you answers.

CHUG:

Maybe it does.

YASSINE:

Tables usually only owe splinters.

Harjeev hears that and still keeps writing.

HARJEEV:

And order.

Don't disrespect the order just because it doesn't flatter you.

ADDY:

He says that like he married the furniture.

HARJEEV:

If I did, at least it would stay where I left it.

Knight finally taps the line beside SOLO.

KNIGHT:

We do Solo next.

Not because he's closest.

Because Riven is using him as a moving lesson.

Every day we wait, that lesson gets harder to reverse.

CHUG:

Then we don't wait.

KNIGHT:

Good.

Try saying it without sounding like a man sprinting into his own funeral.

CHUG:

You're impossible.

KNIGHT:

I'm useful.

Confusion between the two is common.

That almost earns a smile from Addy.

Almost.

[SCENE 2 — THE ROUTE OF FOUR]

Harjeev produces another relay fragment.

Thin slate.

One edge burned.

Two marks on it.

A speed lane symbol and a recovery arrow.

HARJEEV:

Riven's route bends through Cinder Span.

Narrow bridge fields.

Fast cut-roads.

Bad footing.

Perfect for a Nexter who likes turning distance into humiliation.

YASSINE:

So we're walking into a runner's joke.

KNIGHT:

Yes.

Do not become the punchline.

SORYA:

If Riven built the approach honestly, there will be false paths.

If he built it well, the false paths will look kinder.

RAEVAN:

And if he built it like a Nexter, he will attack boredom before he attacks guard.

CHUG:

Meaning?

KNIGHT:

Meaning the first hit happens when you start believing nothing is happening.

Harjeev places fresh supplies on the table.

Bolt racks.

Water salts.

Wrapped med packs.

A compact brace rig.

HARJEEV:

Take this for Chug's side.

And this for Yassine's shoulder.

And if either of you come back pretending those old wounds are small, I will record you as livestock.

YASSINE:

You know, I thought getting rescued would mean more tenderness.

HARJEEV:

And I thought surviving amnesia would make you quieter.

We're both disappointed.

[SCENE 3 — THE STRANGER ON THE RIDGE]

They leave by second shadow.

Chug, Yassine, Knight.

Addy wanted to come.

Knight refused.

Addy argued.

Raevan supported Knight.

Addy argued more.

Harjeev ended it by handing her roof-watch command and calling it a promotion she had not earned yet.

That made her angrier than refusal.

The road to Cinder Span is all broken rails and black grass.

Wind whistles through hollow pipes under the old stone.

By the third rise, Yassine is muttering to himself just to break the silence.

Then a coin hits Chug in the forehead.

Not hard.

Annoyingly accurate.

CHUG:

Ow— what the hell?

A man sits on the ridge above them.

Long coat dusty at the hem.

Hat tipped back.

Hair loose.

Smile much too easy for a road like this.

He flicks a second metal disk between his fingers like the whole world is a stage built for his wrists.

UNKNOWN:

There.

Now I know which one has the thick skull.

YASSINE:

I like him less than Zeph already.

Knight's blade is out before the stranger lands.

UNKNOWN:

Relax, commander face.

If I wanted you dead, I'd have picked a better joke.

He hops down lightly.

Too lightly for a man carrying that many metal discs on his belt.

There is something theatrical about him, but not fake.

Everything he does is balanced on the edge between mockery and precision.

UNKNOWN:

Name's Kais.

CHUG:

Who asked?

KAIS:

No one.

That's why I introduced myself like a civilized menace.

YASSINE:

He's insane.

KAIS:

Not enough to be boring.

Who are you three?

KNIGHT:

No.

KAIS:

Wonderful.

A secretive one.

A serious one.

And—

he points at Yassine—

you move like half your memory went somewhere useful and forgot to send a letter.

YASSINE:

That is aggressively specific.

KAIS:

I try.

CHUG:

We're busy.

KAIS:

So am I.

That's why I found you.

The road ahead is full of speed traps,

false dust,

and one extremely irritating Nexter who thinks style counts as strategy.

I wanted to see if the people chasing him were worth walking beside.

KNIGHT:

And if we aren't?

KAIS:

Then I leave.

Tell a cruel story about you to someone prettier.

And keep moving.

[SCENE 4 — KAIS PROVES HE ISN'T TALK]

Knight does not trust him.

Good.

Chug doesn't either.

Better.

But the road decides before they do.

A line of black wire snaps up from the gravel.

Fast enough to catch ankles and cut tendons if you don't see the shine.

Kais does.

Before the wire finishes rising, he snaps two discs from his fingers.

They spin like flat silver teeth.

One clips the left anchor.

The other hums across the right with such clean angle that the whole trap collapses inward instead of up.

The dust falls.

The road lives.

YASSINE:

...Okay.

CHUG:

Yeah.

KAIS bows slightly.

Too dramatic.

Still deserved.

KAIS:

Thank you.

I practice being impressive because the world keeps rewarding competence too slowly.

KNIGHT watches the discs roll back to Kais's boots and stop there like trained animals.

KNIGHT:

Weapon?

KAIS:

Technique.

Weapons are what frightened people call it first.

He stoops.

Picks up the discs.

Slides them back into the bandolier.

Every motion loose.

Every placement exact.

KNIGHT:

Why help us?

KAIS:

Because the road ahead cut two people I dislike and three I never met.

And because Riven's men took my hat once.

That is not the kind of insult I forgive.

YASSINE laughs before he can stop himself.

YASSINE:

You fought a Nexter over a hat?

KAIS:

No.

I fought him over disrespect.

The hat was just evidence.

That line feels ridiculous.

And somehow solid.

[SCENE 5 — THE FIRST LANE FIGHT]

Riven's runners arrive at dusk.

Not Riven.

Never the first cut.

Only the edges.

Three of them.

Fast.

Light.

Wrist-blade types.

They strike without war cries.

Without threats.

Without anything except speed.

Knight takes center immediately.

KNIGHT:

No chase.

Force the lane.

Chug actually obeys.

That matters.

He pins the first runner's exit with the frame.

Yassine rotates wide.

Kais throws one spinning disk low across gravel and clips the second runner's heel at exactly the moment he thinks the ground is safe.

The third tries to retreat uphill.

Knight is already there.

The fight ends fast.

Too fast to feel good.

Kais crouches by one downed runner and checks the neck mark.

KAIS:

Riven's thread.

Fourth lane.

Tight discipline.

Cruel teacher.

Pretty footwork.

Ugly philosophy.

CHUG:

You know him personally?

KAIS:

Enough to dislike his handwriting on the road.

YASSINE:

That's a weird sentence.

KAIS:

I'm a weird man.

Knight studies the fallen lane mark.

KNIGHT:

Then you're coming.

KAIS tips his hat that he definitely still has.

KAIS:

Now that sounds like trust.

See?

You are improving.

[SCENE 6 — THE ROAD LESSON]

They camp without making camp.

No fire.

No table.

Just a broken culvert and the lee side of old stone.

Kais talks too much.

Yassine answers too quickly.

Knight speaks only when correction is required.

Chug spends more time listening than he used to.

KAIS:

Let me guess.

You are the one who hits problems until they become structure.

CHUG:

That's not what I do.

YASSINE:

That is absolutely what you do.

KNIGHT:

Accurate.

KAIS:

And commander face—

he points at Knight—

is the one who measures grief by how efficiently it can be deployed.

KNIGHT:

Incorrect.

I measure it by whether it destabilizes the line.

Kais grins.

Genuinely pleased.

KAIS:

Even better.

You are impossible.

I enjoy impossible people in controlled amounts.

He looks to Yassine.

KAIS:

And you.

You move like half your memory went somewhere useful and forgot to send a letter.

The joke lands too close.

Yassine goes still.

Kais sees it instantly.

The grin changes.

Softer now.

KAIS:

Sorry.

Wrong cut.

YASSINE:

No.

Just...

true enough to be annoying.

Chug notices that too.

A man who jokes fast and still recognizes where a joke stops being harmless.

That is rarer than style.

[SCENE 7 — SOLO'S MARK]

Near dawn they find the mark.

Not a body.

Not a voice.

A cut in the bridge support at Cinder Span.

Three parallel lines.

One deeper than the others.

A blade signature.

A habit.

A call sign made without words.

Yassine touches it first.

Then withdraws his hand like the stone is warm.

YASSINE:

This is his.

CHUG:

You remember?

YASSINE:

No.

I know.

KAIS studies the cut.

KAIS:

Strong hand.

Decisive.

Impatient enough to insult the bridge while passing through it.

I would've liked him immediately.

KNIGHT:

Then save the opinion until we retrieve the man.

CHUG:

We will.

The bridge answers with a voice from below.

RIVEN:

You say that like retrieval is a direction and not a price.

They all look down.

He is there.

At the lower span.

Lean.

Beautifully balanced.

Cruel without effort.

One hand resting on the shoulder of a man in chains whose head is bowed but whose stance is still somehow proud.

Solo.

Alive.

Not broken.

Not free.

Not yet.
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — THE ROAD THAT CUTS BACK]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

32.text:
[SCENE 1 — SOLO IN CHAINS]

Riven waits below the broken span like he owns gravity.

Maybe he does.

Nexters all look like that when they believe the lane belongs to them.

Solo kneels at his side with one knee chained to a metal brace sunk into the bridge stone.

Not collapsed.

Not helpless.

Just forced into stillness by good mechanics.

That angers Chug more than spectacle would have.

RIVEN:

There.

I told him you'd come loud.

SOLO lifts his head.

His face is thinner than Chug expected.

Harder too.

A cut along the brow.

A bruise yellowing at the jaw.

Eyes clear enough to hurt.

SOLO:

You brought people.

CHUG:

Yeah.

SOLO:

Good.

You finally learned.

That hits Chug harder than Riven's voice does.

KAIS leans over the edge and whistles softly.

KAIS:

I also like him.

Terrible news.

Now I have standards here.

KNIGHT:

Focus.

Riven smiles up at them.

RIVEN:

You can have him.

If you keep what comes with him.

A low sound answers from inside the lower ravine.

Not speed.

Not chain.

Something slower.

Hotter.

SORYA isn't here.

Raevan isn't here.

But Chug still hears Sorya's older warning in memory:

Some enemies do not break courage.

They stain it.

KNIGHT:

Ten.

Riven nods.

Almost politely.

RIVEN:

Zeigran hates waiting.

I told him this bridge would feed him well.

[SCENE 2 — DRACO TEN ARRIVES]

The ravine brightens.

Not with light.

With the color wrongness of old fire refusing to die.

Drako No.10 climbs out of the lower cut without haste.

Armor burnt matte black.

Inner seams glowing like banked coals.

A long blade dragged behind him, not because he needs to, but because the sound eats confidence faster that way.

ZEIGRAN:

So this is the camp's spine.

He looks at Solo.

Then at Chug.

ZEIGRAN:

One chained.

One running.

Good start.

His voice is not loud.

That is what makes it dangerous.

It sounds like it already lives in other people's doubts.

Chug feels something old move under the ribs.

Not fear exactly.

More like remembered failure looking for a chair.

Kais flips one disk through his fingers and mutters without smiling.

KAIS:

Oh.

He burns morale.

I hate those.

You can kill steel.

Mood takes longer.

KNIGHT:

Then do not let him speak long.

RIVEN:

You say that like anyone here controls the conversation.

[SCENE 3 — TWO-FRONT WAR]

It begins all at once.

Riven cuts the upper lines with speed.

Zeigran climbs directly for the center with that quiet dragging blade.

Solo strains at the chain hard enough to split skin.

The bridge trembles under all of it.

Knight chooses first.

KNIGHT:

Chug!

Solo!

Kais with him!

I hold Riven!

Yassine cut the brace!

No debate.

Good.

Chug drops from the upper support to the lower lane.

He lands badly.

Gets up fast.

Kais lands beside him as if the fall was a dance step chosen for style.

KAIS:

This is the worst bridge date I've ever had.

CHUG:

Shut up and move.

Kais grins.

Good.

If he can joke here, his nerve is real.

Zeigran meets them halfway.

Not rushing.

Not needing to.

The air around him already feels like disappointment trying to become law.

ZEIGRAN:

You arrived.

And still feel late.

CHUG doesn't answer.

Good.

Knight's lesson stayed.

[SCENE 4 — ZEIGRAN'S FIRE]

Zeigran's first cut does not seek flesh.

It carves the bridge railing.

Black sparks spray outward and the whole lane fills with heat-haze.

Not enough to burn skin.

Enough to bend certainty.

Suddenly the distance to Solo feels longer.

The chain seems thicker.

Kais's grin looks thinner.

Every next move feels one shade more pointless than it did a heartbeat ago.

Morale burn.

KAIS:

No.

No.

Not buying it.

He snaps two discs into the stone and spins them there.

They hum.

Sing.

Bright metallic sound cutting the oppressive tone like laughter through a funeral line.

The haze shivers.

CHUG:

What was that?

KAIS:

Rhythm.

Bad moods hate rhythm.

Zeigran turns his head slightly.

ZEIGRAN:

Interesting.

That is not praise.

It is target selection.

Kais notices and winks.

KAIS:

Try not to fall in love.

I bruise.

[SCENE 5 — SOLO'S FIRST ANSWER]

Chug reaches the brace line.

Yassine drops from above and hits the chain lock with both blades.

Twice.

Too fast.

Not enough.

Riven sees the attempt and sends a runner-blade down the support cable.

Knight intercepts the blade midline and nearly loses two fingers for the privilege.

Solo finally speaks louder.

SOLO:

Forget the chain.

Break the base!

Chug looks.

The brace isn't holding Solo.

The bridge spine is.

A technique prison.

Not a normal one.

Of course.

CHUG:

Got it.

ZEIGRAN is already on him.

Big cut.

Left to right.

The kind of strike that wants to erase posture and certainty together.

Chug opens Rage 1.

Clean.

Not to overpower.

To shift through.

He slides inside the arc.

Frame-bolt into the lower plate seam.

Yassine dives past him and hits the brace anchor.

Kais throws a spinning disc that hooks the chain ring and forces tension sideways instead of inward.

The brace cracks.

Solo's free knee hits stone.

Then rises.

He rips the chain from his own leg with a sound Chug feels in his teeth.

SOLO:

Took you long enough.

Chug almost laughs.

Almost.

[SCENE 6 — SOLO JOINS]

Solo fights like a rank earned before memory.

Direct.

Heavy.

No wasted courtesy.

Every step insultingly certain.

He picks up the severed chain and uses it as if he trained for exactly this humiliation.

Riven's eyes narrow for the first time.

RIVEN:

There.

That's why I kept you moving.

You stabilize too quickly.

SOLO:

You talk too much.

He hurls the chain.

Riven slips it.

Knight catches the opening and cuts a line across Riven's coat from shoulder to waist.

Not flesh.

Close enough to teach respect.

Riven smiles anyway.

But smaller now.

Zeigran, meanwhile, turns the morale burn harder.

The whole bridge groans under not just weight, but belief failure.

Even Solo's return cannot fully stop it.

ZEIGRAN:

You can free men.

Can you free the room they carry in their chests?

That line nearly lands.

Nearly.

Then Kais claps once.

Sharp.

Bright.

KAIS:

No speeches from the arsonist.

He begins spinning three metal discs on one hand.

A ridiculous trick in a battlefield.

A glorious one too.

The ringing climbs into a pattern and somehow gives everyone a center to hear.

YASSINE:

You're insane.

KAIS:

Yes.

Focus.

[SCENE 7 — RIVEN'S LANE BREAK]

Riven tires of losing rhythm.

He vanishes from Knight's line and appears behind Chug in the lower lane.

Too fast.

Almost.

Solo catches him instead.

Bare forearm to wrist.

Shoulder to chest.

A stop built from stubbornness and old ranking.

SOLO:

Mine.

RIVEN:

Still dramatic.

The two clash at speed.

Not Nexter speed exactly.

But enough to make stone choose a side and regret it.

Knight drops into their lane.

Three lines now.

Not a duel.

An extraction fight becoming execution.

Meanwhile Zeigran raises the long black blade overhead for a bridge-ending cut.

CHUG:

YASSINE!

YASSINE:

I know!

Yassine runs the support rope.

Kais throws all four discs at different points of the lower span.

Each one catches and hums.

Pattern.

Rhythm.

Counter to morale.

Chug uses Rage 1 and the frame together, fires two bolts into the heated seam Zeigran exposed himself.

The black blade drops anyway.

But not clean.

Solo kicks the broken brace section upward.

The falling steel meets Zeigran's cut and changes the angle just enough.

The bridge survives.

The blade doesn't.

Its lower third snaps off and spins into the ravine.

Zeigran finally looks surprised.

Good.

[SCENE 8 — TEN FALLS]

Broken weapons make honest men.

And honest monsters too.

Zeigran throws the ruined blade aside and comes forward with bare gauntlets glowing along the seams.

His morale burn intensifies.

No more words now.

Just pressure.

Just the sensation that nothing done here can last.

Chug understands suddenly.

This is Zeigran's whole doctrine.

Not defeat.

Corrosion.

So he answers the only way that works.

He does not lunge.

He plants.

Calls the line like Knight would.

CHUG:

Solo left!

Yassine low!

Kais sound!

Now!

The order shocks him more than the others.

Because it comes out correct.

Because they move immediately.

Solo takes the left shoulder line and hammers Zeigran's stance open.

Yassine cuts behind the knee.

Kais launches the discs past Zeigran's head and snaps them back in a screaming arc that ruins the morale haze for one crucial breath.

Chug enters on that breath with Rage 1 fully clean and drives the frame-bolt into Zeigran's chest seam at point blank.

Then again.

Then the weighted cord around the glowing gauntlet.

Then elbow through the opened line.

Zeigran drops to one knee amid his own failing heat.

ZEIGRAN:

...There.

The room stopped listening to me.

CHUG:

Yeah.

ZEIGRAN:

Good camp.

He laughs once.

Dark.

Spent.

Not kind.

ZEIGRAN:

Bad for Drakos.

Chug tears the Ten mark free from Zeigran's chest clasp and hurls it into the bridge stone.

SOLO steps beside him.

SOLO:

Finish him?

The question is practical.

Not emotional.

Chug looks at Zeigran.

At the broken bridge.

At Solo free and standing.

At Yassine breathing hard but steady.

At Kais grinning with blood on his sleeve and delight still somehow intact.

Then he looks at Riven.

[SCENE 9 — RIVEN LEAVES WITH A LOSS]

Riven has blood on one wrist now.

Knight put it there.

Solo put two more shallow lines into his shoulder.

For a Nexter, that counts as humiliation.

RIVEN:

You are all becoming inconvenient.

KAIS:

You're welcome.

Riven looks at Solo.

Then at Chug.

RIVEN:

He'll be slower for a while.

I made sure of it.

SOLO:

And you're running now.

I made sure of that.

That lands.

Riven hates landing lines almost as much as losing.

He backs toward the upper lane, not breaking eye contact.

RIVEN:

Keep him then.

But the roads remember ownership.

KNIGHT:

Not anymore.

Riven vanishes into the speed lines he came from.

No dramatic farewell.

Nexters are cowards only when that is efficient.

Zeigran, meanwhile, forces himself back to his feet.

Bleeding from the opened seam.

ZEIGRAN:

Ten falls here.

On a bridge that chose men over momentum.

He takes one step back.

Then another.

CHUG:

Tell Nine we're coming.

ZEIGRAN:

No.

Tell Nine yourselves.

He likes hearing prey sound certain before routes eat them.

Then he is gone too.

Not spared.

Beaten.

And moved off the board.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 32]

Back at camp, Solo arrives with a chain scar still fresh around the leg and a face that looks like sleep and violence have been arguing over it for months.

Harjeev checks the wound first.

Then the pupils.

Then the grip.

Only after all that does he say:

HARJEEV:

Good.

Another expensive person.

SOLO:

Missed you too.

That earns the first real crack in Harjeev's mouth that might one day become a smile.

Yassine drops onto the bench beside Solo.

YASSINE:

Do I know you?

SOLO studies him.

A whole second too long.

SOLO:

Yeah.

YASSINE:

Great.

That's becoming everyone's favorite answer.

Kaizen looks at Chug.

Then at the Ten mark now hanging below Eleven.

KAIZEN:

You ordered well.

Chug hears that harder than the victory.

System text burns low and relentless above the table.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 10 STATUS: DOWN"

"ALLY SOLO — RECOVERY ROUTE OPEN"

"PLAYABLE ROUTE: KAIS AVAILABLE"

"CAMP STRUCTURE LEVEL: EXPANDED"

[BOSS GATE — Nexter No.5 Riven]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for NO.4 RIVEN / NO.10 ZEIGRAN.

33.text:
[SCENE 1 — SOLO IN CAMP]

Solo does not re-enter life gently.

He re-enters it like a door forced on old hinges.

He sits at the table on the first morning with the chain scar visible and his patience gone.

Harjeev hands him food.

Solo eats like someone who remembers starvation more clearly than rescue.

Knight gives him no comfort.

Raevan gives him a training blade before a greeting.

Kaizen ignores him on purpose.

Yassine keeps staring at him like recognition might climb up through the eyes if he waits long enough.

SOLO:

You going to blink eventually or is this a test?

YASSINE:

Maybe both.

SOLO:

Good.

You were annoying before too.

YASSINE:

That actually helps.

Chug watches them and feels something ugly loosen a fraction inside his chest.

Not relief.

Not yet.

But a version of it learning to sit upright.

ADDY:

He's got the same face you used to make at ranked rooms.

SOLO glances at her.

SOLO:

Addy.

ADDY:

Yeah.

SOLO:

You still shoot like apology is beneath you?

ADDY:

Recovered enough to prove it.

That passes for affection here.

Good enough.

[SCENE 2 — SOLO'S RESIDUE]

Raevan runs Solo through basic motion tests.

Not because Solo needs basic training.

Because rescued fighters need proof that their body belongs to them again.

Solo passes every test too aggressively.

Footwork.

Reaction.

Grip.

Chain transfer.

Directional break.

He has not forgotten how to fight.

He has only forgotten how to stop.

RAEVAN:

Enough.

SOLO:

No.

RAEVAN:

Enough.

SOLO finally lets go of the practice dummy's arm.

The wood is cracked in three places.

HARJEEV, writing:

Add one dummy to the list of Solo's emotional expenses.

SOLO:

Manager still alive.

Shame.

HARJEEV:

Rank still intact.

Tragedy.

Yassine laughs outright.

That seems to startle Solo more than any blade test did.

SOLO:

You really don't remember?

YASSINE:

No.

SOLO:

Huh.

YASSINE:

What?

SOLO:

You laughed easier before things got bad.

That lands softly.

Still hard.

[SCENE 3 — NINE'S COUNTRY]

Knight drops a new route shard on the table.

Different from Riven's.

Different from Zeigran's.

It is carved like a forked road that keeps eating itself.

KNIGHT:

Nine.

CHUG:

Morvain.

KNIGHT:

Route eater.

Territory consumer.

He does not break camps by impact or morale.

He turns movement itself against you until every path leads where he wants.

SORYA:

A hungry map.

HARJEEV:

Awful phrase.

Accurate phrase.

SOLO studies the shard.

SOLO:

I've seen this work.

Not him.

His country.

Roads that loop.

Safe paths that shorten into cages.

Retreats that become deliveries.

KNIGHT:

Where?

Solo closes one fist slowly.

SOLO:

Transfer south.

Before Riven.

They moved a woman through one of Morvain's corridors.

Didn't show her face.

Didn't need to.

Everyone kept using the initials like it was enough.

O.O.

Chug looks up.

Addy too.

ADDY:

O.O?

SOLO:

Yeah.

YASSINE:

That's a person?

SOLO:

Girl.

Mean enough to survive people talking about her like a weapon.

Addy almost smiles.

ADDY:

I think I already like her.

[SCENE 4 — SIGNAL IN THE GLASS]

That evening a light begins blinking from the far watch stones.

Not camp code.

Not Drako pressure.

Not Nexter thread.

Three long.

Two short.

Three long.

Pause.

Repeat.

Addy sees it first.

ADDY:

Signal.

Knight is already on the ridge.

KNIGHT:

Source?

ADDY:

East mirror line.

High angle.

Not random.

Solo comes up behind them.

SOLO:

Neon.

CHUG:

NeonKd?

SOLO nods once.

SOLO:

Only one I know who'd send code into hostile light and trust ego to carry it through.

The signal shifts.

Different pattern now.

Directed.

A message more than a ping.

Sorya narrows her eyes at the flashing.

SORYA:

It is bouncing through dead reflective planes.

Whoever is sending this understands ruined glass.

Addy starts translating by instinct.

Not because anyone taught her at camp.

Because residue is cruelly helpful.

ADDY:

"Silence Gallery.

North vault.

Road false.

Take the broken left."

...

She stops.

Breath catches.

ADDY:

And...

"She's still cutting them."

The whole table understands.

O.O is alive.

Somewhere inside Morvain's route country.

Still making enemies bleed inside a system built to erase direction.

[SCENE 5 — KAIS BECOMES CAMP]

Kais has stayed.

No one asked him to.

No one fully told him to leave either.

He just started helping repair things badly and then well and eventually the camp gave up pretending he was temporary.

He now sleeps near the south wall with one boot on and one off as if commitment is a negotiable joke.

Harjeev hates his storage habits.

HARJEEV:

Why are there metal discs in the water basin.

KAIS:

Because if I put them near my bed,

Yassine steals them.

YASSINE:

I was looking.

KAIS:

With criminal posture.

Harjeev pinches the bridge of his nose.

Kais spins a disc over the back of one hand and drops it into the map table cup exactly upright.

KAIS:

That said,

the signal route is good.

Too good.

If Neon sent it,

someone wants us to receive it.

KNIGHT:

Of course.

KAIS:

No.

I mean someone smart enough to leave one truth inside three lies.

That's not routine work.

That's personal architecture.

CHUG:

Morvain.

KAIS:

Probably.

Or whoever he uses to decorate the corridors.

Either way,

this is going to be a rude walk.

[SCENE 6 — PLAYABLE STATUS AND THE SEAT]

Harjeev updates the board after dark.

ADDY — ACTIVE

YASSINE — ACTIVE

KAIS — ACTIVE

SOLO — LIMITED / RECOVERY

Solo sees the word LIMITED and gives Harjeev a look sharp enough to cut paper.

SOLO:

Change that.

HARJEEV:

No.

SOLO:

I can fight.

HARJEEV:

Yes.

You can also overextend,

bleed through the old restraint line,

and become a hero in exactly the useless way Knight keeps beating out of Chug.

Knight does not look up from the map.

KNIGHT:

Manager is correct.

SOLO:

I hate all of you.

KAIS:

Wonderful.

That means you're family already.

Solo actually almost laughs.

Almost.

That is how everyone knows Kais has some impossible social weapon beyond steel.

[SCENE 7 — THE ROAD TO SILENCE GALLERY]

They leave at low gray.

Chug.

Yassine.

Addy.

Kais.

Knight.

Solo stays furious at camp, which Harjeev correctly identifies as the safest version of him today.

The road to Silence Gallery feels wrong before it looks wrong.

Footsteps echo half a second late.

Broken signs point in mutually exclusive directions.

Birds do not cross the same line twice.

Kais tosses a disc down one "safe" lane.

It vanishes.

No sound.

No bounce.

KAIS:

Not that one.

YASSINE:

How are you still so calm?

KAIS:

Because panic ruins style.

KNIGHT:

And because he is competent enough to decorate his recklessness.

KAIS tips the hat he is somehow still wearing.

KAIS:

I feel seen.

Addy studies the blink-reflections on the ruined gallery walls.

ADDY:

Neon's path starts left.

Then fakes right.

Then cuts under.

He's leaving us a route inside Morvain's route.

That's either genius or grief.

CHUG:

Move on genius first.

No one argues.

[SCENE 8 — SILENCE GALLERY]

The Gallery is a dead museum for sound.

Marble halls.

Collapsed mirrors.

Black curtains hanging from nowhere.

Every step swallowed too fast.

Every word feeling expensive.

Morvain's territory.

The first corridor forks three ways.

Then four.

Then one again.

Then the floor changes texture and everyone stops.

KNIGHT:

Don't trust any route that becomes convenient after resistance.

KAIS:

He says things like that and somehow still isn't fun at parties.

YASSINE:

Have you ever seen him at a party?

KAIS:

No.

I'm proving my own point.

A cut appears on the wall ahead.

Three circles.

One slash through two of them.

Addy's face changes.

ADDY:

That's hers.

CHUG:

O.O?

ADDY:

Yeah.

Legend O.O.

She marks kills with circles.

Near misses with lines.

That means two dead.

One kept moving.

KAIS:

Oh I absolutely like her.

[SCENE 9 — THE GIRL THEY CALLED A WEAPON]

They find her in the north vault.

Not chained.

Not kneeling.

Standing.

One shoulder against a broken column.

One eye half-covered by a torn black cloth.

Twin narrow blades in reverse grip.

Boots blood-dark to the ankle.

Around her are five corridor bodies.

Every one of them cut at the exact joint where movement dies fastest.

She is breathing hard.

Still ready.

O.O:

You took too long.

Addy actually laughs this time.

ADDY:

Yeah.

You too.

O.O's gaze shifts over the group.

Measures everyone.

Stops on Chug.

Then Yassine.

Then Kais.

O.O:

You brought a clown.

KAIS:

A stylish professional.

Please insult accurately.

She almost smiles.

Almost.

Then the walls begin to move.

Not physically.

Spatially.

Morvain noticed them.

O.O straightens off the column and blood runs from her sleeve.

O.O:

Good.

Now we find out if you're worth the route you came in on.
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — THE GIRL CALLED O.O]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

34.text:
[SCENE 1 — MORVAIN CLOSES THE HALL]

Silence Gallery seals behind them without doors moving.

That is how they know Morvain is near.

The corridors begin folding preference into space.

Distances shorten only when walked wrong.

Turns appear familiar until someone chooses them.

Voices come from ten feet away and three halls over at the same time.

Morvain does not enter like the other Drakos.

He enters as absence choosing shape.

MORVAIN:

Good.

The famous camp finally walked inside my mouth.

No body yet.

Only the voice.

Smooth.

Patient.

Predatory in a manner that thinks patience is elegance.

O.O rolls her shoulder once and ignores the blood.

O.O:

You talk like a hall monitor who learned murder.

KAIS:

Oh, she's excellent.

CHUG:

Can you fight?

O.O looks at him like the question offended her lineage.

O.O:

Can you keep up?

That answers itself.

[SCENE 2 — O.O IN MOTION]

When the first route-wraiths come,

O.O moves before anyone else.

Not flashy.

Not loud.

Not emotional.

Precise.

Deadly.

Economical.

She cuts the lead wraith at the hip turn.

Uses the falling body as cover.

Reverse grips into the next throat seam.

Kicks the third off the corridor lip and never watches it fall.

KAIS:

Yes.

Absolutely yes.

ADDY:

Told you.

YASSINE:

She's terrifying.

O.O:

Correct.

She says it without arrogance.

Which is somehow colder.

Knight watches her lines once and nods.

KNIGHT:

Anchor killer.

Good.

O.O:

Finally.

A useful man.

Kais clutches his chest theatrically.

KAIS:

And here I thought I was winning you over.

O.O:

You are a noise source.

KAIS:

I've been called worse by prettier women.

O.O's knife almost flicks toward him on reflex.

Addy catches the motion and smirks.

Good.

That means some tension here may one day become trust.

[SCENE 3 — MORVAIN'S MAZE]

The Gallery route folds around them.

The "broken left" path Neon sent remains valid for exactly forty steps,

then becomes a drop into a glass pit.

Knight halts them one breath before disaster.

KNIGHT:

Back.

Kais tosses a disc.

No return.

KAIS:

Rude architecture.

ADDY:

No.

Adjusted architecture.

He's listening to the route as we move.

CHUG:

Can he do that?

SORYA's teaching answers in memory.

Some fields don't just hold space.

They rewrite permission.

O.O kneels.

Touches a line of blood she'd left earlier on the floor.

O.O:

Then we use what he didn't author.

CHUG:

Meaning?

O.O:

Pain is honest.

He can eat roads.

Not wounds already spent.

She drags her own blood mark across the floor in a deliberate line.

The corridor doesn't change under it.

Knight sees immediately.

KNIGHT:

Good.

Trail your certainties.

No assumed paths.

Kais grins.

KAIS:

I really do love serious people.

They keep turning suffering into method.

YASSINE:

That's a terrible sentence.

KAIS:

Yet useful.

[SCENE 4 — NEON'S SECOND SIGNAL]

A flash pulses through the mirrors again.

Different from the east watch.

Closer.

Sharper.

ADDY:

Neon.

The mirrored code bounces through three cracked surfaces and resolves just long enough to read.

"LOW CHAMBER.

CUT SOUND.

NINE LIKES STILLNESS."

O.O curses softly.

O.O:

He pinned Neon under the listening floor.

CHUG:

Then we move.

KNIGHT:

No.

We move correctly.

Morvain's voice folds through the hall again.

MORVAIN:

Still pretending there is a difference.

That line almost makes the next step feel futile.

Almost.

Kais snaps two discs together.

The ringing cuts the mood sink in half.

KAIS:

There.

Now he's only half annoying.

O.O side-eyes him.

O.O:

You're ridiculous.

KAIS:

And alive.

Watch how often those overlap.

[SCENE 5 — LOW CHAMBER]

The chamber below is built like an inverted bell.

Sound falls to its center and dies there.

The floor is latticed glass over black machinery.

At the center,

half-buried in a signal frame,

is NeonKd.

Wires across the spine.

Pulse visor over one eye.

Hands locked into two broken relay grips.

He sees them first through the visor reflection.

NEONKD:

You picked the wrong left.

ADDY actually laughs in relief.

ADDY:

Shut up, Neon.

NEONKD:

Aw.

So it is my people.

His smile is tired.

Still there.

Then the floor shakes.

Morvain finally steps into sight above them on the highest gallery bridge.

Tall.

Lean.

Armor carved like route lines crossing over each other.

Face hidden behind a half-mask split vertically like two roads refusing to agree.

MORVAIN:

You are all very sentimental for people who keep surviving geometry.

CHUG:

Get down here.

MORVAIN:

Why?

The whole room already belongs to me.

[SCENE 6 — NINE'S REAL POWER]

Morvain doesn't attack with force.

He attacks with options.

He tilts one hand.

Half the floor becomes farther.

The other half becomes easier than it looks.

The support beams trade places in the eye.

O.O's blood trail is the only honest thing left in the room.

NEONKD:

Don't trust the shine!

Trust the heat signatures!

Left-middle is fake!

Right-low is also fake!

Oh that's very rude—

A glass spear nearly takes his throat before Addy shoots it out of the air.

ADDY:

Still talking too much.

NEONKD:

Means I lived.

Knight is already mapping the true load lines.

KNIGHT:

O.O on blood path.

Chug with her.

Yassine and Kais cut the upper angle.

Addy suppress Morvain's hand line.

I free Neon.

No one hesitates.

Good.

That is camp work,

not hero work.

[SCENE 7 — O.O SHOWS WHY SHE'S LEGEND]

O.O takes point.

Not because Chug yields it.

Because she is already there.

She walks the blood path like a woman stepping across names she stopped fearing years ago.

Every false panel trying to invite her somewhere easier.

Every invitation ignored.

Morvain finally sounds interested.

MORVAIN:

There you are.

The girl who kept cutting exits instead of making them.

O.O:

And you're the thing that thinks roads matter more than who survives them.

MORVAIN:

They do.

O.O:

Then you're a coward with architecture.

She reaches the first support pillar and hammers both reverse grips into the route seam.

The room shudders.

For one breath,

one whole section tells the truth again.

Chug uses that breath.

Rage 1.

Frame-bolt.

Upper bridge support.

Kais throws spinning steel along the outer rail and lets the return path ricochet through four false openings just to prove he can.

He clips Morvain's mask seam.

KAIS:

Hello from below.

Morvain doesn't even look at him.

Which is insulting enough to work.

YASSINE:

He hates you.

KAIS:

Excellent.

So does gravity most days.

[SCENE 8 — FREEING NEON]

Knight reaches Neon through the true lower lane.

Neon is laughing under pain.

Which feels like exactly the wrong response until Knight gets close enough to hear the strain in it.

NEONKD:

If I stop joking,

the room wins.

KNIGHT:

Then keep joking and give me the lock order.

Neon blinks once.

Twice.

NEONKD:

Left wrist relay.

Spine release.

Then visor.

Not visor first.

Never visor first.

Knight obeys without comment.

Good.

This is not the hour for ego.

Addy covers from the side.

Three arrows.

Three redirected route shards.

One almost impossible save.

Addy and Neon were clearly friends before all this.

You don't cover like that unless someone once made your whole bad day survivable.

The lock tears free.

Neon gasps.

Almost folds.

Still energyges:

NEONKD:

Took you all forever.

I would've been out in twenty more minutes.

ADDY:

No you wouldn't.

NEONKD:

Yeah.

Probably not.

[SCENE 9 — NINE FALLS]

Morvain sees the room slipping out of his control and stops pretending patience is enough.

He drops from the upper bridge into the chamber itself.

Bad idea.

Necessary one.

Chug meets him.

O.O catches the left route.

Yassine kills the retreat seam.

Kais turns the outer reflections into noise.

Addy keeps the pressure off Neon and Knight while they drag the signal frame clear.

Morvain fights beautifully.

That makes him infuriating.

No wasted motion.

No blind rage.

Just exact cruelty.

He almost gets Chug with a false near step that turns into a side cut.

O.O intercepts with both blades crossed and takes the hit across one forearm instead of Chug's throat.

CHUG:

You good?!

O.O:

Fight.

Good answer.

Chug does.

He changes rhythm the way Knight forced him to learn.

Not direct.

Not loud.

He lets Morvain think the next path exists,

then kills it himself.

Yassine sees it.

Kais sees it.

They all hit the same broken possibility.

O.O locks the torso line.

Yassine cuts the rear knee.

Kais breaks the balance with a ricochet spin to the heel plate.

Chug drives the frame-bolt straight through the split route mask.

Morvain falls backward through his own false path.

His field flickers.

Then dies.

The whole chamber gasps its geometry back into place.

MORVAIN:

...Ugly.

You made it ugly.

CHUG:

Good.

MORVAIN:

Nine doesn't die in pretty rooms.

He tears the route insignia from his collar and lets it clatter across the blood-streaked floor.

MORVAIN:

Then let Eight judge your formations.

He vanishes through a route collapse before anyone can decide mercy or execution.

Cowardly.

Efficient.

Very Nine.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 34]

Back at camp,

the table receives two new names in living form.

O.O sits with her arm stitched and her patience gone.

O.O:

This place better have standards.

HARJEEV:

It has ledgers.

Close enough.

Neon lies half-propped against the med post with one eye still light-sensitive and both hands still twitching like they want signal grips back.

NEONKD:

Nice camp.

Bad walls.

Mid food.

HARJEEV:

Recover first.

Then insult with full data.

Solo looks at O.O.

Then Neon.

Then Chug.

SOLO:

Roster's getting real.

Knight nails the Nine mark beneath Ten.

Then marks two lines on the board.

O.O — ACTIVE ROUTE OPEN.

NEONKD — RECOVERY / SIGNAL.

Kais drops into the empty seat opposite Tora's ring and grins when Harjeev glares.

KAIS:

What?

I'm temporary.

But dramatically.

System text burns brighter than usual.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 9 STATUS: DOWN"

"ALLY O.O — PLAYABLE STATUS OPEN"

"ALLY NEONKD — RECOVERY ROUTE OPEN"

[BOSS GATE — Drako No.7 Dread Juno]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for NINE EATS ROADS.
SYSTEM: BOSS — DRAKO NO.7 DREAD JUNO

35.text:
[SCENE 1 — CAMP TOO FULL TO FAIL]

Camp is louder now.

Not noisy.

Alive.

Solo and Yassine argue through drills.

Addy and O.O compete without admitting they are doing it.

Neon gives route advice from the med shade and insults everybody's timing despite barely standing straight.

Kais somehow turns supply sorting into a card trick and nearly gets stabbed by Harjeev for it.

Knight has stopped trying to prevent this and started using it as morale.

That is more frightening than the tricks.

Chug stands at the table and understands what Tora meant.

A camp is not comfort.

It is capacity.

HARJEEV:

Do not look sentimental at the board.

It weakens the wood.

CHUG:

You're impossible.

HARJEEV:

No.

You all just think affection should be soft.

It shouldn't.

It should stay through repairs.

That line belongs on the table more than any trophy does.

[SCENE 2 — EIGHT'S PRESSURE]

Eight begins without courtesy.

Not a voice in stone.

Not weather.

Not route lies.

Formations break.

Random challenger groups that should move like mobs start moving like units.

Flank lines tighten without visible commanders.

Ambushes come from mathematically correct angles.

Retreats bait exactly the wrong responder out of sector.

Knight identifies it after the third near breach.

KNIGHT:

Eight.

Kaith.

Formation breaker.

O.O wipes her blades.

O.O:

So he doesn't hit hardest.

He rearranges people until they become weak.

KNIGHT:

Yes.

KAIS:

Rude profession.

RAEVAN:

Effective profession.

Chug studies the board.

Every rescue so far has widened the camp.

That also means there is more to disrupt.

Good.

Harder.

Real.

GUIDE:

Eight will attack your confidence in each other.

CHUG:

Then he gets nothing.

GUIDE:

No.

He gets attempts.

You remove payoff.

Subtle difference.

Useful one.

[SCENE 3 — THE CARRIAGE IN THE CUT]

Harjeev's outer watch whistles twice at dusk.

Different code.

Medical code.

No enemy horn follows it.

Knight is moving before the second whistle dies.

Chug,

Yassine,

Solo,

and O.O follow.

Addy takes roof cover.

Neon stays with the signal stones.

Kais comes because Kais comes.

They reach the north cut and find a broken transfer carriage lodged against black stone.

No horses.

No beasts.

Just drag channels.

Meaning it was pulled by men or worse.

The carriage is burned on one side and sealed on the other with med script nearly scraped away.

HARJEEV arrives seconds later,

breath already irritated.

HARJEEV:

Move.

If that's a live transfer,

every heartbeat we waste is criminal.

They cut the seals.

Inside is one man.

Half-conscious.

Chest bound badly.

Side wound reopened.

Forearm wrapped in old pressure cloth.

Face pale from blood loss and stubbornness.

M.R.

Chug knows it instantly.

Before memory explains.

Before logic catches up.

The rank lives in the body.

Same as the name did.

CHUG:

...M.R.

The man's eyes force half-open.

Sharp.

Even through the pain.

M.R:

Took...

you... long enough.

Then he passes out again.

Yassine looks between them.

YASSINE:

That's him?

Chug can't answer immediately.

Because yes.

Because the answer is bigger than the voice.

Because the man looks worse than the med note implied and somehow even injured still gives off the feeling of a first-rank presence trying not to inconvenience anyone with pain.

HARJEEV:

Stop staring.

Lift him.

The spell breaks.

Good.

Camp before feeling.

Again.

[SCENE 4 — BACK TO CAMP WITH WEIGHT]

The return is careful and ugly.

O.O clears the route.

Solo carries the front corner of the improvised stretcher.

Chug takes the rear.

Yassine shadows the flank.

Knight watches for pursuit.

Kais keeps talking just enough to stop everyone sinking too deep into the tension.

KAIS:

You know,

this is exactly how all great friendships begin.

Injury.

Silence.

A suspiciously handsome stranger on a stretcher.

O.O:

If you flirt with the dying,

I'll stab you on principle.

KAIS:

That's the most promising response yet.

Solo actually snorts.

M.R remains unconscious.

But somehow the tension lightens half a degree.

Useful idiot.

That might be Kais's whole category.

[SCENE 5 — M.R UNDER HARJEEV'S HAND]

Harjeev takes command of the med line like a general takes walls.

HARJEEV:

Addy,

boil water.

O.O,

lamp.

Knight,

cut the old wraps.

Chug,

if you stand there being emotional,

I'll bill you for lost time.

Chug moves instantly.

Good.

The wound is worse than it looked.

Rib-side entry.

Burned edge.

Old internal shock.

Three reopened stitches.

Bruising that suggests transport without mercy.

Neon squints from the signal corner.

NEONKD:

He got transferred through bad roads.

No clean med route would make that bruising.

Harjeev grunts.

HARJEEV:

Correct.

Whoever moved him cared more about destination than condition.

YASSINE:

Enemy?

KNIGHT:

Not sure.

O.O:

Then assume yes until proved useful.

Harjeev cuts the old bandage away and freezes just long enough for Chug to notice.

CHUG:

What?

HARJEEV:

This stitch pattern.

Everyone waits.

HARJEEV:

Camp work.

Not enemy work.

Someone tried to keep him alive properly before the transfer broke.

That changes the room.

Not enough to become hope.

Enough to become complication.

[SCENE 6 — M.R WAKES]

He wakes at midnight.

Of course he does.

Men like that never choose a convenient hour.

Chug is the only one still awake at the med post.

That feels like destiny until Harjeev shouts from the next room for more water and ruins the mood.

M.R's eyes open clear despite the pain.

That is the first frightening thing about him.

The second is that he assesses the room before he speaks.

M.R:

Camp.

CHUG:

Yeah.

M.R looks at him.

Really looks.

And the old hierarchy Chug felt in the name becomes real.

Not because M.R is cruel.

Because presence itself is organized differently around him.

M.R:

You look worse with responsibility.

Chug laughs before he means to.

A real laugh.

Too sudden.

Too honest.

CHUG:

Good to see you too.

M.R:

Would've stood for the greeting.

Side disagreed.

The pain hits him then.

You can see it try to take his breath.

He does not let it own his face.

Chug notices.

That too is familiar.

CHUG:

Don't talk.

M.R:

No.

You finally found me.

I'm absolutely going to talk.

Yassine,

from a nearby blanket:

He sounds like he belongs here.

Annoying.

M.R turns his head a little.

Studies Yassine.

Something unreadable moves behind the eyes.

Then gentleness.

Unexpectedly.

M.R:

You stayed.

YASSINE:

Apparently that's my whole reputation.

M.R almost smiles.

Then the pain kills the attempt.

M.R:

Good reputation.

[SCENE 7 — WHO M.R IS NOW]

By morning everyone has met him.

Harjeev hates that he sat up before permission.

Knight hates that he clocked the sector layout in one glance.

Addy hates that he immediately recognized her draw shoulder injury from posture alone.

O.O hates that she does not hate him on sight.

Kais loves him in under thirty seconds for the same reason everyone else becomes careful:

M.R looks wounded and still somehow radiates command without trying.

KAIS:

Oh.

You're a dangerous one.

M.R,

dry:

Says the man wearing absurd confidence as outerwear.

KAIS clutches his chest in delight.

KAIS:

I adore him.

Solo watches from the wall.

Silent.

Hard to read.

M.R sees him too.

M.R:

You look like you broke a chain with attitude.

SOLO:

You look like med forgot to finish the job.

M.R:

True.

Still prettier though.

That finally cracks the room.

Even O.O looks away to hide the laugh.

Even Harjeev gives up pretending not to appreciate competent insolence.

[SCENE 8 — EIGHT TESTS THE CAMP]

Kaith's first direct strike comes while M.R can barely stand.

Not a big attack.

Worse.

A precise one.

Three challenger units hit three sectors at the exact same time:

south brace,

signal corner,

med line.

Formation break.

Not casualty hunt.

Trust break.

Knight reacts immediately.

But the camp is half a breath off.

One breath is enough for Eight.

O.O moves to signal.

Addy covers south.

Solo and Yassine cross to med.

Chug goes center.

Kais goes where the noise is worst because of course he does.

M.R rises from the med cot anyway.

HARJEEV:

Sit down before I nail you there.

M.R:

No.

Wrong rotation.

The room pauses.

Because wounded men do not usually sound correct enough to stop trained fighters.

M.R points.

M.R:

Solo,

don't cross med.

Hold the seam between med and signal.

Yassine,

left ladder to Addy's lane.

Kais,

if you're going to be chaotic,

do it on the south flank where it helps.

Chug,

center isn't center today.

Take the cut behind the brace and kill the hinge unit.

Knight watches him.

One second.

Then:

KNIGHT:

Do it.

And everyone does.

Because M.R was right.

The attack collapses in under forty seconds.

Kaith did not break the camp.

He learned it.

That may be worse.

[SCENE 9 — KAITH'S MESSAGE]

One of the dead challengers carries a pinned plate on the inside of the armor.

Not a full mark.

A lesson tag.

HARJEEV reads it.

"GOOD CAMP.

BAD HABIT.

YOU STILL TURN TOWARD THE LOUDEST DAMAGE."

M.R holds out a hand.

Harjeev gives him the plate without comment.

M.R reads once.

Then looks directly at Chug.

M.R:

He's right.

No malice.

No softness either.

Just the kind of truth only high-ranked friends ever got away with saying before the world ended.

CHUG:

I know.

M.R nods once.

Satisfied.

Or maybe just unsurprised.

YASSINE:

I feel like he got introduced already being everyone's problem.

KAIS:

Best kind of introduction.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 35]

That night Harjeev updates the board.

M.R — MED / ACTIVE MIND

NEONKD — SIGNAL LIMITED

O.O — ACTIVE

SOLO — RECOVERY ACTIVE

KAIS — ACTIVE

Chug sees it and realizes how strange the camp has become.

Names that were once rumors are now arguing over ration salt and sector assignments.

Guide speaks low over the last lantern.

GUIDE:

Careful.

Some returns arrive exactly when they can do the most damage.

Chug looks at M.R asleep upright against the med wall,

as if even unconscious he refuses to fully let go of the room.

CHUG:

Yeah.

But he does not sound convinced.

System text flickers like a held breath.

SYSTEM:

"ALLY M.R. — ARRIVED"

"DRAKO 8 PRESSURE ACTIVE"

"CAMP STATUS: STRAINED BUT INTACT"
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — MED TRANSFER]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

36.text:
[SCENE 1 — THE WOUNDED MAN WHO GIVES ORDERS]

M.R should be resting.

Harjeev says this four times before breakfast.

M.R still ends up at the table.

Not because he wants to dominate it.

Because people keep unconsciously leaving him the clearest angle.

That bothers Chug when he notices.

Then bothers him more when he notices why:

because it feels natural.

M.R studies the board once and immediately points at the sectors Kaith touched.

M.R:

He doesn't want our walls.

He wants our instincts.

If we keep answering noise with the same body shifts,

he'll split us where habits live.

Knight folds his arms.

KNIGHT:

Go on.

M.R:

Rotate false command twice a day.

Swap med lane and signal lane guards.

Make Harjeev call one wrong order in drills and punish whoever follows it automatically.

Force people to check,

not obey.

Kaith is reading reflex.

Harjeev is offended on principle.

HARJEEV:

I am not calling wrong orders in my own camp.

M.R:

Then call "test order" and punish speed anyway.

Same result.

More dignity.

Harjeev thinks.

Hates that he is thinking.

Finally nods.

HARJEEV:

Fine.

But if you collapse the stitches doing my work,

I'm charging you for the bandages.

Kais claps quietly.

KAIS:

Oh, this man is criminally useful.

O.O:

He's exhausting.

YASSINE:

Both can be true.

[SCENE 2 — KAITH SHOWS HIS FACE]

By noon Kaith finally appears in person.

Not like Arowh.

Not like Varkul.

Not like Morvain.

He arrives inside a formation.

Six challengers in exact spacing.

Three support shooters.

Two chain hookers.

One shield front.

Kaith in the hollow center.

Armor layered in sharp black geometry.

Every plate built to direct the eye somewhere wrong.

Twin batons at the hips.

Face hidden behind a segmented visor that makes even stillness look like tactic.

KAITH:

Better.

The camp has begun to think.

M.R doesn't rise.

He only watches from the table edge with a hand pressed to the stitched side.

M.R:

And he hates that.

Kaith hears him.

Tilts the visor.

KAITH:

Transferred alive.

Poor energygement on our side.

The room goes colder.

Not because of Kaith.

Because of the way M.R does not react outwardly at all.

He files that line away instead of bleeding on it.

That is more dangerous than anger.

CHUG:

You touch him again,

you don't walk away.

KAITH:

No.

If I touch him again,

your camp turns around itself before I need to finish the job.

That is Eight's whole doctrine.

Make the group cut itself open.

[SCENE 3 — FALSE ORDER DRILL BECOMES REAL]

Harjeev had just begun the false-order drill when Kaith arrived.

Good.

Bad.

Useful.

HARJEEV:

South line fall back—

No.

Hold.

Test order.

Hold your actual sectors!

The challengers hit exactly then.

Which means Kaith had been reading the camp from before he showed himself.

Half the newer fighters almost move wrong.

Almost.

M.R's voice cuts the air.

Not loud.

Absolute.

M.R:

Ignore noise.

Watch Knight's hand.

Knight doesn't even flinch.

He simply raises two fingers and shifts them left.

Everyone who should understands.

The line holds.

Kaith notices.

Again.

KAITH:

There.

The wound talks.

M.R:

And you still don't understand what that means.

[SCENE 4 — CAMP FIGHT / FORMATION WAR]

This is the cleanest enemy assault yet.

That makes it horrifying.

No screaming.

No berserk rush.

No dramatic pressure.

Just correct violence applied at correct intervals.

Addy takes the first support shooter through the eye slit.

O.O and Solo break the hookers before the med line gets entangled.

Yassine rotates to the left seam and catches the second shooter from below.

Kais turns one flank by making his spinning discs ricochet off the watchpost rails in a pattern nobody sane would predict.

The pattern works anyway.

KAIS:

I call this "respectfully impossible."

O.O:

You call everything something stupid.

KAIS:

And yet you keep using it.

She does.

That matters.

Chug drives for Kaith.

Stops halfway.

Because M.R had told him earlier:

If Eight wants center,

deny him prediction instead of speed.

So Chug veers.

Kills the shield front first.

Not glamorous.

Correct.

Kaith sees it.

Adjusts.

Too late.

Knight enters the opening.

[SCENE 5 — M.R IN COMMAND]

Harjeev is still running triage and sector allocation,

but the fight has two command centers now:

the Manager for logistics,

M.R for battle pattern.

That should be impossible.

Instead it works.

M.R:

Neon,

ping the false east route now.

Neon is still technically limited.

Still half-recovering.

Still immediately obeys.

NEONKD:

On it.

Signal stones flash east.

Kaith's back pair reorients for a flank that doesn't exist.

Addy punishes the turn.

Two arrows.

Two dropped supports.

M.R:

Solo,

don't chase.

Cut return.

SOLO:

Already there.

M.R:

Kais,

make noise south then break north.

KAIS:

That's rude.

I love it.

He does exactly that.

Kaith's formation bends wrong for one precious second.

M.R:

Chug.

Now.

Chug moves.

Rage 1 clean.

No waste.

No blind fury.

Just sharpened acceleration.

He collides with Kaith at the gap the whole camp just built for him.

That feels different from the old days.

Better.

Less lonely.

More deadly.

[SCENE 6 — KAITH'S BREAK]

Kaith fights like architecture with fists.

Every strike trying to force Chug back into predictable lanes.

Every pivot setting the field for the next collapse.

Chug doesn't take the bait.

He lets Solo and O.O own the edges.

Lets Addy close sight lines.

Lets Yassine cut the retreat seam.

Lets Knight take the opposite shoulder.

For the first time Kaith's formation discipline turns into a cage around himself.

KAITH:

...There.

CHUG:

Yeah.

There.

Kaith whips a baton across Chug's jaw and nearly steals the sentence with it.

Chug answers with the frame under the baton guard.

Point blank.

Center seam.

Kaith staggers.

Yassine is in immediately.

Low cut.

High reverse.

O.O hits the wrist line from the blind side.

Knight drives a short blade into the segmented visor gap.

Kaith drops to one knee.

Not dead.

Worse for him.

Aware.

KAITH:

You have a camp now.

M.R answers from the table.

Still wounded.

Still upright.

Still impossible to ignore.

M.R:

Yes.

Kaith turns his head slowly toward the sound.

KAITH:

Then it will hurt more when Six gets his teeth into it.

M.R's face does not change.

M.R:

He'll choke.

That line chills even Kaith.

Good.
