Chug tears the Eight mark from Kaith's chest harness and lets it fall into the dirt between them.

CHUG:

Leave.

Kaith rises with hard precision even while bleeding.

KAITH:

You think mercy is structure.

Interesting mistake.

KNIGHT:

No.

We think message travel is useful.

Kaith studies them all once more.

Then withdraws in perfect backward order.

Even defeated,

still formatted.

[SCENE 7 — THE THING ABOUT M.R]

After the field quiets,

everyone looks toward M.R without meaning to.

That is the thing about him.

He doesn't ask for center.

He becomes one.

Harjeev notices it too.

You can tell because he hates it more professionally than everyone else.

HARJEEV:

Back on the cot.

Now.

M.R:

No.

HARJEEV:

That was not a debate.

M.R finally grimaces as the side wound catches up.

He sits because the body leaves him no graceful alternative.

KAIS,

softly to Yassine:

He's good enough to be annoying on moral grounds.

YASSINE:

Yeah.

I noticed.

O.O watches M.R with the same unreadable severity she gave Knight when he first arrived.

O.O:

You command like you knew all of us before we got cut apart.

M.R looks at her.

Then at the table.

Then away.

M.R:

Maybe I did.

No one pushes further.

Not because they are kind.

Because they all feel the line around that answer.

[SCENE 8 — NEON RETURNS PROPER]

Neon comes down from the signal post under his own power for the first time after the fight.

Still shaky.

Still bright-eyed.

Still too smart for his own safety.

NEONKD:

Can I officially complain now?

Because I hate being "limited."

HARJEEV:

No.

NEONKD:

Can I complain anyway?

HARJEEV:

Yes.

Complaining is not a combat role.

Knight marks the board.

NEONKD — ACTIVE SIGNAL / FIELD LIMITED removed.

NEONKD — ACTIVE.

Neon sees it and goes very still for one second.

Then:

NEONKD:

Nice.

ADDY:

Yeah.

NEONKD:

Okay.

That's actually nice.

That kind of admission costs him.

Which means camp has him more firmly now.

[SCENE 9 — END OF 36]

At night Harjeev updates the ledger.

DRAKO NO.8 — KAITH

DEFEATED

Neon active.

Solo route stable.

O.O active.

Kais active.

M.R med-active.

Addy active.

Yassine active.

Chug very active and very annoying.

Harjeev does not say the last one aloud.

But he writes something that suspiciously looks like it.

Guide speaks over the quiet.

GUIDE:

Six does not attack walls.

Six attacks movement after decision.

Knight answers before Chug can.

KNIGHT:

Then we prepare to be hunted.

M.R opens one eye from the cot.

M.R:

No.

We prepare to make the hunt expensive.

That lands like old rank speaking through new pain.

System text burns cold and certain.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 8 STATUS: DOWN"

"ALLY NEONKD — FULL ACTIVE STATUS"

"CAMP STATUS: MULTI-COMMAND VIABLE"

[BOSS GATE — Nexter No.4 Rhaziel]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for EIGHT BREAKS, CAMP HOLDS.

37.text:
[SCENE 1 — TOO MANY ACTIVE NAMES]

The board is crowded now.

Chug.

Yassine.

Addy.

Solo.

O.O.

NeonKd.

Kais.

Knight.

Harjeev.

M.R.

Tora's ring.

Two marks still waiting farther down the line.

REE.

FRIEND.

Camp has become the kind of place losses return to.

That is beautiful.

That is dangerous.

That is exactly why Seven comes.

Juno's first sign is not an attack.

It is a missing patrol.

Two outer scouts fail to return.

Then a third.

No bodies.

No blood.

Just route silence.

Knight goes colder than usual.

That is saying something.

KNIGHT:

Seven.

CHUG:

Dread Juno.

KNIGHT:

Pursuit collapse.

Hunter doctrine.

He doesn't crack camps.

He peels people away until camp cracks itself reaching after them.

M.R,

still pale but upright:

Then no one leaves alone.

Not even to piss on a wall.

Harjeev points with the pen.

HARJEEV:

Finally.

A sentence I want carved into wood.

YASSINE:

He's fitting in disturbingly well.

ADDY:

I know.

I hate how easy it feels.

O.O:

Easy is not the word.

She doesn't finish the thought.

Doesn't need to.

[SCENE 2 — KAIS AND M.R]

Kais finds M.R near the med shade before noon,

working a route diagram with one hand because the other side still hurts too much to fake strength convincingly.

KAIS:

You do realize resting is a sacred art.

M.R:

I rest when structure holds without me.

KAIS:

Ah.

One of those.

M.R glances up.

M.R:

And you're one of those.

KAIS:

The charming kind?

Yes.

M.R:

The kind that smiles when thinking gets dangerous.

Kais grins,

caught exactly enough to enjoy it.

KAIS:

I knew you were my kind of headache.

He drops into a seat opposite and spins one disc across the table.

M.R stops it without looking,

two fingers clean on the edge.

KAIS:

Well now.

That was rude.

M.R:

No.

That was accurate.

They look at each other for one long second.

Different men.

Different energies.

Both impossible in different directions.

Kais is delighted.

M.R almost is.

[SCENE 3 — SOLO'S ACTIVE RETURN]

Knight finally removes Solo's LIMITED marker.

Not ceremonially.

Just with the knife tip.

SOLO notices anyway.

SOLO:

About time.

KNIGHT:

Prove me right.

SOLO:

I plan to.

YASSINE:

What does Solo fight like when he's fully awake?

ADDY:

Like a door deciding violence was a language.

SOLO:

Accurate.

RAEVAN hands Solo a chain-sickle hybrid built from camp parts and old restraint metal.

RAEVAN:

You liked the chain when you were angry.

SOLO tests the weight.

It settles.

Good.

SOLO:

Yeah.

This works.

M.R watches the exchange from across the yard.

M.R:

No flourish on the second pull.

You'll open your own shoulder.

Solo turns toward him.

SOLO:

You remember that?

M.R:

I remember winning arguments with you.

Same muscle group.

That lands with the old familiarity of people who used to rank each other without needing numbers explained.

[SCENE 4 — FIRST PURSUIT LOSS]

The first true Juno strike happens on a supply run that should have been too small to matter.

Exactly why it matters.

Harjeev sent two load-bearers and one guard to the east cache.

They never reach it.

Not dead.

Worse.

Found later hanging from a route tree under black cords with their weapons arranged in a circle around them.

Alive.

Shaking.

Unable to explain how far they ran before realizing they were running in someone else's direction.

Juno doesn't kill.

He teaches panic.

Harjeev stares at the recovered guard for a long time.

HARJEEV:

No more small runs.

KNIGHT:

Agreed.

CHUG:

Then we bait him.

KNIGHT:

Yes.

But not like a hero.

Like a hunter.

That difference is everything.

[SCENE 5 — O.O GETS REAL]

O.O volunteers first.

O.O:

Use me.

Silence answers.

Not refusal.

Calculation.

O.O:

He wants motion with edges.

I am motion with edges.

Use me.

Addy studies her.

Then nods once.

ADDY:

I'll cover.

YASSINE:

I'll shadow.

SOLO:

I'll close the back cut.

KNIGHT:

No.

Everyone looks at him.

KNIGHT:

We do not feed Seven one sharp fighter and call it strategy.

We build him a pursuit he can't finish.

M.R,

from the med post:

Then pair O.O with Kais.

That gets immediate reactions.

O.O:

No.

KAIS:

Yes.

M.R ignores both.

M.R:

Seven wants seriousness to isolate itself.

Give him one blade he can read,

and one disaster he can't.

Kais puts a hand to his chest,

offended and delighted at once.

KAIS:

I am a crafted man,

not a disaster.

O.O:

You're both.

Knight thinks one second.

Then nods.

KNIGHT:

Done.

O.O hates it.

Which means it is probably correct.

[SCENE 6 — HUNT BAIT]

The bait route begins at dusk.

O.O and Kais take the visible track.

Deliberately.

Addy high cover.

Yassine ghosting the lower path.

Solo cutting rear return.

Chug and Knight holding the choke point where pursuit should become overconfidence.

Neon in signal relay.

Harjeev coordinating fallback.

M.R at the table despite everyone pretending they don't notice they keep checking whether he's still upright.

Juno comes invisible at first.

Then the signs.

Broken reeds pointing the wrong way.

One thrown knife left where only O.O would see it.

A coin Kais dropped returned to his pocket without him noticing.

KAIS:

Oh,

now that's personal.

O.O:

Stop smiling.

KAIS:

Can't.

I'm being professionally courted.

Then the first cut lands.

Not on flesh.

On Kais's coat hem.

A warning.

A measurement.

JUNO:

Too loud.

The voice is close.

Then far.

Then behind.

Then nowhere.

O.O doesn't answer.

Good.

She learns fast.

Kais answers anyway.

KAIS:

And you're too shy.

That gets him a second cut.

Across the hat brim this time.

KAIS:

Unforgivable.

[SCENE 7 — DREAD JUNO APPEARS]

He finally shows when Kais deliberately trips one false line and pretends worse balance than he has.

Juno drops from an overhead support with no wasted shadow.

Lean.

Long-limbed.

Dark pursuit harness packed tight to the body.

No heavy armor.

No unnecessary plates.

Just movement engineered to become fear.

Twin hooked knives.

Mask smooth as old bone.

One red stitch line running vertically from forehead to chin.

DREAD JUNO:

The clown was bait.

Unexpectedly decent bait.

KAIS:

Thank you.

I'm also available for weddings.

O.O is already moving.

Juno expected that.

He expected Kais too.

What he does not expect is the distance between them not staying honest,

because Addy and Neon have already altered the chase arcs with signal pings and arrow impacts.

Knight's trap begins.

[SCENE 8 — JUNO'S HUNT REVERSED]

Yassine closes the lower route.

Solo drops the rear chain line.

Chug and Knight rise from the choke seam.

For the first time in a long while,

the hunter is the one inside the pattern.

Juno doesn't panic.

That makes him worthy of the rank.

He smiles under the mask anyway.

You can hear it.

DREAD JUNO:

Better.

Now someone here understands movement.

KAIS:

We have several someones.

Very inconvenient for you.

The fight is vicious and narrow.

No room for speeches.

Only pursuit physics.

Chug misses once and Juno is already at his flank.

O.O takes the angle.

Kais ruins the next line with a spinning ricochet Juno couldn't predict.

Yassine's blade catches cloth.

Solo's chain-sickle catches the hook line.

Addy's arrow forces the leap earlier than Juno wanted.

Knight turns the early leap into a bad landing.

Juno is still terrifying.

Still nearly impossible to hold.

Still finally in danger.

He takes a cut across the side.

Then another.

Then a frame-bolt through the outer thigh.

He laughs.

DREAD JUNO:

There.

You learned.

CHUG:

Yeah.

Now stay down.

Juno doesn't.

Of course he doesn't.

He rips the bolt free and backs through the pursuit lane in perfect retreat order.

KNIGHT:

No chase!

Everyone obeys.

Good.

That is new too.

Juno pauses at the last dark seam.

DREAD JUNO:

Six will starve you better than I can.

I was sent to see if you know how to keep names from running after ghosts.

He touches the cut in his side.

Looks at the blood.

Then at O.O and Kais.

DREAD JUNO:

Interesting pair.

Then he is gone.

[SCENE 9 — END OF 37]

Back at camp,

Harjeev writes without looking up.

JUNO — NOT DOWN.

PATTERN LEARNED.

Chug reads that and frowns.

CHUG:

Not down?

HARJEEV:

Not down.

You asked for accuracy.

Managers remember.

M.R,

from the cot:

Good.

Then we don't mistake one wounded hunter for a won route.

O.O cleans her blades.

O.O:

I still hate him.

KAIS:

Excellent.

Hatred with standards is the beginning of teamwork.

O.O:

If you say one more thing like that,

I'll remove your smile by hand.

Kais grins wider.

System text burns low but not victorious.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 7 STATUS: ACTIVE / WOUNDED"

"ALLY SOLO — FULL ACTIVE STATUS"
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — JUNO HUNTS]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

38.text:
[SCENE 1 — THE HUNTER COMES BACK]

Juno does not wait long.

Wounded hunters rarely do.

Pain makes some men cautious.

It makes others impatient.

Dread Juno belongs to the second kind.

Three nights after the first trap,

the camp lights die in sequence.

North.

South.

West.

Not by wind.

By cut.

Then the signal stones blink emergency red.

NEONKD:

He's inside the outer rings!

Everyone moves before Knight speaks.

Good.

Then Knight speaks anyway.

KNIGHT:

Sector hold!

No lone pursuit!

Juno wanted panic.

He gets structure.

Bad trade for him.

[SCENE 2 — M.R REFUSES THE COT]

Harjeev physically blocks M.R's way as the wounded man tries to rise.

HARJEEV:

No.

M.R:

Move.

HARJEEV:

Still no.

M.R puts one hand on the table to steady the side wound and looks at him with the kind of patience that outranks anger.

M.R:

If Seven is inside the rings,

a static brain is more useful than a resting body.

Harjeev hates that sentence because it is true.

HARJEEV:

Then sit.

And command from there.

If you tear those stitches,

I will recover you personally just to shout while sewing.

M.R actually inclines his head.

Compromise accepted.

That too is a kind of leadership.

[SCENE 3 — THE CHASE THROUGH CAMP]

Juno moves through camp like an accusation.

Fast.

Precise.

Never where the fear says he should be.

Always where the line almost thins.

He cuts one rope support.

Then a water sling.

Then a signal cord.

Tiny damages.

Cumulative panic.

Addy tracks him from the roof.

Misses once on purpose because the angle isn't clean.

Hits the second time when O.O forces the lane.

Solo seals the south gap.

Yassine rotates.

Kais throws noise into the dark like he is conducting an invisible orchestra.

KAIS:

Come on,

grave-face!

If you're going to stalk us,

at least commit artistically!

Juno answers by nearly taking Kais's ear off.

KAIS:

See?

Personal growth.

O.O:

You are exhausting.

[SCENE 4 — M.R'S CALL]

The whole camp starts over-rotating toward one cut lane.

Exactly what Juno wants.

M.R sees it from the table first.

M.R:

Stop turning center!

He's baiting weight through memory!

Hold your first assignments!

That line snaps the whole pattern back into shape.

Chug hears the call and obeys instantly.

So does Solo.

So does O.O.

Even Addy shifts target priority without needing it repeated.

Juno notices.

Of course he does.

He appears atop the med awning for one heartbeat just to look at M.R.

DREAD JUNO:

You.

M.R's face does not move.

M.R:

Me.

Something unreadable passes between them.

Recognition?

History?

A line from a road Chug never walked?

Not time to ask.

Good.

Questions are expensive during hunts.

[SCENE 5 — THE LAST CHASE]

Knight changes the camp pattern mid-fight.

Not spoken.

Hand signs.

The camp answers.

Yassine and O.O become the forward blades.

Solo and Chug become the walls closing behind pursuit.

Addy takes Juno's exits.

Kais ruins whatever elegance remains.

This time when Juno cuts through the east brace,

he finds not panic,

but prepared emptiness.

No one there.

No momentum to steal.

He lands in a kill box.

DREAD JUNO:

...Good.

O.O is first.

Knife to wrist.

Not deep.

Exact.

Yassine second.

Low cross to ankle.

Chug third.

Rage 1 burst into center.

Solo fourth.

Chain-sickle across retreat lane.

Addy fifth.

Arrow through cloak tie,

pinning motion to air for half a second.

Kais only laughs.

KAIS:

There.

Now it's a proper party.

That half second is all Knight needs.

He steps in and cuts Juno's mask cleanly from brow to mouth.

The mask splits.

Falls.

Juno's face beneath is younger than Chug expected.

Tired.

Sharp.

Almost beautiful in the wrong way.

A hunter made into doctrine before he had time to become a man.

DREAD JUNO:

Should've left when Seven said go.

CHUG:

Should've stayed gone when we said no.

Frame-bolt.

Point blank.

Shoulder seam.

Juno drops.

[SCENE 6 — SEVEN FALLS]

He does not try to rise fast this time.

Only once.

Once is enough to prove the spine is still made of hunt.

Then Solo's chain locks the wrist.

O.O's blade settles at the throat.

Addy's arrow finds the heartline.

Knight stands over the center.

Juno looks up at all of them.

Not angry.

Not broken.

Evaluating to the end.

DREAD JUNO:

You built the camp right.

That's why this hurts.

M.R's voice carries from the table even now.

M.R:

Then remember it while leaving.

Juno laughs once.

Small.

Almost respectful.

DREAD JUNO:

So that's where they put you.

That line freezes the air harder than blood does.

Chug hears it.

Files it.

Does not turn.

Good.

A month ago he would've ruined the moment.

Not now.

Juno unclasps the Seven mark himself and lets it fall.

DREAD JUNO:

Tell Six starvation is harder when the meal starts hunting back.

He withdraws under his own feet.

Slowly.

Not because he wants dignity.

Because the camp took speed from him.

That matters more.

[SCENE 7 — THE QUESTION NO ONE ASKS PROPERLY]

After the lights are restored and Harjeev has finished insulting everyone back into calm,

Chug finds M.R still at the table,

breathing a little too carefully.

CHUG:

He knew you.

M.R:

Yes.

CHUG:

From where?

M.R:

Roads.

CHUG:

That's not an answer.

M.R:

It's the one you get tonight.

Chug hates that.

Which means he believes it enough not to force the rest.

Annoying restraint.

Useful restraint.

YASSINE,

sitting nearby with a fresh wrap on one forearm:

You really do talk like the room belongs to you.

M.R glances at him.

M.R:

No.

I talk like I prefer rooms not to fall apart.

KAIS,

from the other side of the table:

Same thing in better shoes.

That actually gets a tired look from M.R that might one day become friendship.

Might.

[SCENE 8 — END OF 38]

Harjeev updates the ledger.

DRAKO NO.7 — DREAD JUNO

DEFEATED

Then,

after a long pause,

a second note:

M.R — KNOWN TO ENEMY COMMAND

He doesn't explain why he wrote it.

Doesn't need to.

Everyone sees it.

No one comments first.

Because that line is a future knife.

Not tonight's.

Kais leans back in the chair and tips his hat over one eye.

KAIS:

Good camp.

Terrible sleep quality.

O.O:

Leave if you're tired.

KAIS:

No.

I just got invested.

System text burns clear.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 7 STATUS: DOWN"

"ALLY O.O — FULL ACTIVE STATUS"

"THREAT NOTE: ENEMY RECOGNIZES M.R."

[BOSS GATE — Drako No.6 Tyrvak]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for SEVEN DOWN.

39.text:
[SCENE 1 — AFTER THE HUNTER]

Camp should feel safer after Seven falls.

It doesn't.

That is how they know Six is worse.

Attrition doesn't announce itself with spectacle.

It enters through numbers.

Sleep debt.

Food count.

Arrow stock.

Frayed cord.

Old wounds reopening.

People choosing the shorter walk because the longer one costs too much.

Harjeev notices first.

Of course.

HARJEEV:

Water down one crate.

Bolt stock low.

Bandage cloth insufficient for another big field.

And somebody keeps stealing salt.

Everyone looks at Kais.

KAIS:

I cook better with seasoning.

HARJEEV:

You burn water.

KAIS:

Only when distracted beautifully.

No one laughs.

That is the problem.

The camp is tired.

Six feeds on tired.

KNIGHT:

Rhaziel.

CHUG:

Attrition lord.

KNIGHT:

He won't rush.

He'll make every victory cost twice what it paid.

M.R,

softly:

Then we stop spending like frightened men.

Everyone looks at him because the sentence is too correct to ignore.

[SCENE 2 — RHaziel's method]

The first Rhaziel crew doesn't attack walls.

It attacks supplies in motion.

A med courier half-route gets intercepted.

Not killed.

Stripped.

Left alive with one message pinned to the empty pack frame.

"STARVE BETTER."

Harjeev reads it,

folds it once,

and says nothing for a dangerous amount of time.

Then:

HARJEEV:

No more linear supply runs.

Everything rotates.

Everything doubles back.

No container leaves camp without false cargo.

No one travels without a second purpose.

Knight nods once.

KNIGHT:

Good.

Chug watches Harjeev then.

Really watches.

The man isn't just keeping lists.

He's keeping war from becoming panic through accounting.

That matters.

Maybe more than blades on days like this.

[SCENE 3 — M.R STEPS INTO THE WORK]

M.R can stand longer now.

Not fully.

Enough.

He refuses field duty.

Correctly.

Instead he takes the table apart and rebuilds the whole route board into sections:

food,

med,

signal,

fighter readiness,

false routes,

true routes,

bait routes.

HARJEEV stares.

HARJEEV:

You've done this before.

M.R:

Yes.

HARJEEV:

At this scale?

M.R:

Worse.

That line should mean comfort.

Instead it raises ten more questions.

Neon watches M.R adjust signal priorities.

NEONKD:

You think like a person who moved groups,

not just friends.

M.R doesn't look at him.

M.R:

Friends are just groups you bleed for faster.

That answer is honest enough to make the room quieter.

[SCENE 4 — RHazIEL'S FACE]

Six arrives on the third day of shortage.

No grand entrance.

No cliff silhouette.

He simply walks with the next stripped convoy like he has always been part of the line.

Rhaziel is tall in the way famine is.

Not massive.

Wasting.

Long dark coat over armor built like overlapping blade-thin ribs.

A hooked polearm in one hand.

The other holding a water ration skin he tears open and pours into the dirt while watching the camp.

Everyone hates him instantly.

Good.

Some enemies earn it clean.

RHAZIEL:

You rebuilt faster than your stores did.

Prideful choice.

HARJEEV actually steps forward before Chug does.

HARJEEV:

You touch another crate,

I skin you down to arithmetic.

Rhaziel smiles.

Thin.

Cruel.

Interested.

RHAZIEL:

Ah.

The man who understands war in honest units.

M.R rises from the table behind Harjeev.

Still pale.

Still not fully healed.

Still enough.

M.R:

And the parasite who mistakes thinning a line for superiority.

Rhaziel's gaze shifts.

RHAZIEL:

There you are.

Again.

Enemy recognition.

Again.

Chug feels the board under his ribs change.

Again.

[SCENE 5 — SIEGE INSIDE THE PERIMETER]

Rhaziel doesn't storm the camp.

He enters it like scarcity made flesh.

Behind him,

six lean attrition crews spread to exactly the points where camp repairs are newest.

They know what to cut because they've been taught what cost the most to replace.

KNIGHT:

All sectors hold.

No chase.

No loose heroics.

We win by keeping more than we spend.

That is Six's fight.

Resource against resource.

Structure against hunger.

Addy and O.O take alternating high lines.

Yassine and Solo work the moving kill seams.

Kais and Chug rotate impact response.

Knight runs center.

Harjeev and Neon protect the stores and signal grid.

M.R refuses the cot and takes the board.

HARJEEV:

You tear the side open and I swear on every ledger I own—

M.R:

Then keep me alive and complain later.

Harjeev hates that he cannot argue.

[SCENE 6 — CAMP BURNS SLOW]

The fight drags.

That is what Rhaziel wants.

Not seconds.

Minutes.

Every minute costs cloth.

Water.

Breath.

Focus.

Rhaziel's crews never overcommit.

They damage and withdraw.

Damage and withdraw.

If Addy fires,

they change cover.

If Yassine kills one,

another steals the med minute.

If Chug crushes a flank,

Rhaziel takes a ration line.

It is infuriating.

It is brilliant.

KAIS,

while deflecting a hooked blade with a spinning disc:

I hate competent cruelty.

It has no sense of theater.

RHAZIEL,

from three sectors away:

And yet you keep performing.

KAIS:

Someone has to improve the scenery.

The joke buys Yassine one second.

Enough to keep a med strap from being cut.

Sometimes Kais's ridiculousness is a combat contribution.

Annoying.

Useful.

Camp logic.

[SCENE 7 — M.R IN FIELD LIMITS]

Then the worst thing happens.

The signal grid gets hit.

Neon takes a cut across the hand.

Harjeev loses the med count in a spilled crate.

Knight is tied up center.

Chug is too far left.

And Rhaziel turns toward the table.

Straight toward M.R.

Everyone sees it.

No one gets there in time.

RHAZIEL:

You command from furniture now?

How diminished.

M.R is already standing.

One hand to the side wound.

One knife in the other he somehow had before anyone noticed.

Of course he did.

M.R:

Still enough.

Rhaziel attacks.

Fast for a man that lean.

The polearm not swung wide.

Needled.

Precise.

Built to make movement expensive.

M.R does not win the exchange.

He survives it.

That matters.

One step back.

Table edge to redirect.

Knife to shaft.

Chair kick to lower balance.

No wasted panic.

Only bought time.

Time is what the camp needs.

Chug sees the line and opens Rage 1 so hard Kaizen would hate it if he were closer.

Too late to hate.

Good enough to matter.

He crosses the whole center lane and hits Rhaziel before the second killing line lands.

The table splits.

The strike doesn't.

[SCENE 8 — STARVING SIX]

Now Rhaziel has Chug in front,

Kais at one side,

Solo and Yassine closing,

O.O and Addy controlling his exits,

Knight cutting the only honest retreat,

Harjeev screaming inventory numbers like curses,

Neon rebuilding the signal lane one-handed,

and M.R still upright behind the broken table because some men are too proud to collapse on schedule.

Rhaziel hates this.

Good.

RHAZIEL:

You spent too much to get here.

M.R answers first,

voice rough from the wound and the refusal to yield:

M.R:

Wrong.

We invested.

That line lands on everyone.

Not just Rhaziel.

Even Harjeev hears it.

And Harjeev loves a sentence that turns survival into math without killing its soul.

Knight takes the cue.

KNIGHT:

Collapse the polearm line!

Addy pins the outer grip.

O.O severs the sling tie.

Solo catches the shaft with chain.

Yassine cuts under the elbow seam.

Kais ricochets a disc off the shattered table into the knee lock.

Chug drives the frame-bolt straight through the exposed rib-plate junction.

Rhaziel folds around the hit.

Not dramatically.

Hungrily.

Like he's still trying to count whether the camp paid too much even while losing.

Chug takes the Six mark from his chest harness himself.

CHUG:

Wrong again.

Rhaziel spits blood at the dirt.

RHAZIEL:

Maybe.

But your stores are still lower than your pride.

HARJEEV,

immediately:

Not after I inventory your convoy.

That is such a Harjeev line that even Rhaziel goes still for one second.

Good.

That second is enough.

Knight's blade at throat.

No chase.

No overkill.

No foolishness.

Rhaziel withdraws because the board says he lost.

Not because mercy moved him.

That is fine.

Victory doesn't need his feelings.

[SCENE 9 — WHAT M.R COST]

When the field finally quiets,

M.R sits down too fast.

The side wound opened.

Not badly.

Enough.

Harjeev is on him immediately.

HARJEEV:

You impossible bastard.

M.R:

Useful bastard.

HARJEEV:

That is not a defense.

M.R:

It should be.

Harjeev is too busy saving him to answer.

Chug kneels on the other side.

Too angry to speak properly.

M.R notices.

Of course he does.

M.R:

Don't.

CHUG:

Don't what?

M.R:

Turn this into guilt.

I stood because it was correct.

That answer feels old.

Familiar.

High-rank friend old.

The kind that used to settle arguments by saying the sharpest truth first.

Chug hates how much he missed that voice before he knew he had.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 39]

The camp survives Six.

Not gracefully.

Not cheaply.

But properly.

Harjeev inventories the captured convoy by lantern light.

Water.

Med cloth.

Salt.

Oil.

Needle packs.

Three spare bowstrings.

One signal battery.

Two ration crates.

And a set of black med clamps stamped with transfer code.

M.R sees those clamps and goes very still.

Too still.

Only Chug notices.

That matters too.

No question yet.

Not tonight.

Harjeev writes:

DRAKO NO.6 — RHAZIEL

DEFEATED

Below it:

CONVOY CAPTURED

LOSS ACCEPTABLE

TABLE DESTROYED / REBUILD REQUIRED

Kais rests both boots on the broken remains of the old table and grins into the smoke.

KAIS:

Well.

If you're going to build a legend,

at least you picked entertaining methods.

System text burns like tired iron.

SYSTEM:

"DRAKO 6 STATUS: DOWN"

"RESOURCE SWING: POSITIVE"

"M.R. CONDITION: WORSENED / STABLE"
[EXPANDED ENCOUNTER — SIX STARVES]\nSIDE ROUTE CLASH. The chapter breathes through another live combat beat instead of cutting early.

40.text:
[SCENE 1 — AFTER SIX]

Camp smells like splintered wood,

hot metal,

medicine,

and survival expensive enough to be respected.

The old table is gone.

In pieces.

Used as brace,

cover,

weapon,

and sacrifice.

Harjeev mourns it like a competent soldier.

That is to say:

he doesn't.

He rebuilds.

HARJEEV:

No one talk to me until this leg is level.

KAIS:

Is that a threat or a prayer.

HARJEEV:

Both.

The captured convoy changed everything.

For the first time since early camp,

the stores are not an emergency.

Med is stocked.

Water stable.

Bolts and strings sufficient.

Signal gear doubled.

Even Harjeev's handwriting looks less violent.

That,

more than Rhaziel's fall,

tells Chug Six truly lost.

[SCENE 2 — REBUILD AS RITUAL]

Everyone helps rebuild the table.

Not because Harjeev orders it.

Because everyone now understands what the table means.

Knight sets the frame.

Raevan levels the braces.

O.O carves new sector notches.

Addy sands arrow guides into the edge for quick pickup.

Yassine and Solo carry the slab top together while insulting each other the whole time.

Neon wires the signal inlays under the rim.

Kais engraves tiny spinning-disc marks into the underside where only he and Harjeev will ever know they exist.

Harjeev pretends not to know and complains anyway.

M.R should not be standing.

Harjeev says so hourly.

M.R still fits the new route markers into the board one-handed because the camp keeps unconsciously checking his face before major decisions and nobody wants to admit what that means yet.

Chug notices.

Again.

Doesn't like how much he doesn't dislike it.

GUIDE:

He organizes attention.

CHUG:

Yeah.

GUIDE:

And you let him.

CHUG:

Should I not?

Long pause.

GUIDE:

Decide later.

That answer is useless.

Which means it is probably dangerous.

[SCENE 3 — M.R AND THE CLAMPS]

At dusk,

when the others are carrying planks,

Chug finds M.R alone with the black med clamps from Rhaziel's convoy.

He is turning one over carefully.

Not like loot.

Like memory he never wanted back.

CHUG:

You recognized those.

M.R doesn't deny it.

M.R:

Transfer rig hardware.

CHUG:

From what happened to you?

M.R:

From where I was before the cut-road broke.

CHUG:

Can you tell me?

M.R looks at the clamp a second longer.

Then sets it down.

M.R:

I can tell you pieces.

A convoy.

Bad road.

Wrong escort.

Someone in the line deciding I was worth moving even wounded.

Someone else deciding the road mattered more than the body.

Then noise.

Then break.

Then less than memory and more than pain.

Then you.

That answer is not enough.

It is also more than Chug expected to get.

He accepts it because camp has taught him some truths need more structure than hunger.

CHUG:

You remember us?

M.R looks up at him.

The eyes are tired.

Still sharp.

M.R:

Enough.

CHUG:

Enough for what?

M.R:

Enough to know you got older where it matters.

And worse where it shows.

Chug laughs despite himself.

CHUG:

You really are you.

M.R:

Bad news for everyone.

[SCENE 4 — SOLO, O.O, ADDY, YASSINE]

The roster feels real now.

Solo runs live chain drills with Yassine and almost smiles when Yassine finally anticipates the third pull.

O.O and Addy compete at impossible knife-into-arrow sequences across the yard and refuse to call it a competition.

Neon has fully infested the table signal system and now claims the board hum "sounds more honest."

Kais keeps appearing in the wrong sectors and somehow improving them by accident.

Knight tolerates him with increasing strategic resignation.

Harjeev hates everyone equally and therefore fairly.

Raevan and Kaizen remain the closest thing the camp has to old mountains.

Chug watches all of it and understands the act changed.

This is no longer rescue after rescue.

This is camp becoming faction.

Good.

Necessary.

Terrifying.

[SCENE 5 — WHO IS LEFT]

Harjeev reads the remaining unrecovered names aloud while the second table dries under lantern heat.

REE.

FRIEND.

Only two left on the unresolved board now.

Two names for the next act.

Two absences that change the shape of the room whenever silence lasts too long.

Addy traces one fingertip along Friend's line.

Neon taps Ree's tag twice against the wood like old code.

Solo looks at neither.

Yassine looks at both as if staring harder might grow memory.

M.R studies the board.

Then says the sentence no one wanted first.

M.R:

If we keep expanding without closing the holes,

the camp becomes too wide to trust.

Knight nods once.

KNIGHT:

Correct.

O.O folds her arms.

O.O:

Then we close the holes next.

Chug looks around the table.

At the people already back.

At the empty seats still waiting.

CHUG:

Yeah.

We do.

[SCENE 6 — KAIS BECOMES PLAYABLE PROPER]

Kais has been here long enough that temporary stopped fitting three jokes ago.

Raevan tosses him a camp-forged set of six weighted spin coins with sharpened rims and grip grooves.

RAEVAN:

Stop using bent scavenged metal.

You're making the yard look unserious.

Kais catches the set and goes very still for exactly one second.

KAIS:

You made these?

RAEVAN:

I corrected them.

The camp made them.

Kais turns one between his fingers.

Tests the balance.

Smiles,

but not the usual easy one.

Something smaller.

Truer.

KAIS:

Well.

Now I have to stay.

HARJEEV:

You were already staying.

We just hadn't billed you rent yet.

SYSTEM:

"ALLY KAIS — FULL PLAYABLE STATUS CONFIRMED"

YASSINE:

Congratulations.

You're officially a problem on our side.

KAIS:

The finest kind of citizenship.

[SCENE 7 — M.R'S SEAT]

Night falls.

The second table is finished.

Bigger.

Heavier.

Reinforced with convoy steel.

Signal wire under the edges.

New seat marks.

Recovery hooks at the rear.

A med drawer Harjeev insisted on.

A hidden disc slot Kais definitely added.

No one proves it.

Chug takes Tora's ring from the old place and sets it at the new table edge.

Then the Ten,

Nine,

Eight,

Seven,

Six marks below.

Then the carved M.R line from the ruined first table.

He pauses.

Everyone watches.

Not because ceremony matters.

Because placement does.

He sets the carved line into a real seat marker.

Not at the head.

Not hidden.

Near the table's strategic side.

Close enough to command.

Far enough not to eclipse the whole room.

M.R sees it.

Says nothing for a while.

Then:

M.R:

You don't have to do that.

CHUG:

Yeah.

I do.

M.R looks at the seat.

Then at the room.

Then away.

M.R:

Dangerous decision.

HARJEEV:

Most useful ones are.

Knight does not object.

That matters more than approval.

[SCENE 8 — GUIDE'S SHADOW]

Later,

when the others thin out and the lanterns go lower,

Guide speaks from somewhere above the rebuilt structure.

GUIDE:

Seats change wars.

M.R's eyes lift toward the dark.

Only a fraction.

Almost invisible.

Enough for Chug to notice.

M.R:

Depends who sits in them.

GUIDE:

Exactly.

The room stills in a strange way.

Not hostile.

Not peaceful.

Recognizing.

Like two knives hearing each other across cloth.

Chug notices.

Files it.

Says nothing.

Not because he isn't curious.

Because camp has taught him timing.

Still,

the feeling stays.

Guide and M.R know edges of the same dark.

Maybe.

Enough to matter later.

Not enough to fracture now.

[SCENE 9 — THE NEXT HORIZON]

Neon patches one last signal stone into the table and the map lights under their hands.

Knight marks the current field.

DRAKOS DOWN:

12

11

10

9

8

7

6

Routes remaining for the next act.

Fewer numbers.

Worse names.

Higher consequences.

And on the ally side:

Chug.

Yassine.

Addy.

Solo.

O.O.

NeonKd.

Kais.

M.R.

The camp is no longer "a place."

It is now a roster that can move.

That means the war changes.

It also means the losses ahead will hurt in more directions.

Solo breaks the quiet first.

SOLO:

Only two names left before the next wall.

ADDY:

Ree.

Friend.

O.O:

Then we take them.

M.R folds his hands once over the table edge.

M.R:

Not with momentum.

With discipline.

Higher ranks won't give us retrieval windows this generous again.

KAIS:

So less improvisation?

Awful philosophy.

KNIGHT:

No.

Precise improvisation.

Try to keep up.

Kais grins.

KAIS:

That I can do.

[SCENE 10 — END OF 40]

When the camp finally sleeps,

Chug stands alone before the second table.

Not with loneliness.

With responsibility.

Different weight.

Better one.

He looks at the board.

At M.R's new seat.

At Tora's ring.

At the names still waiting.

At the Drako marks already taken.

At the camp that now knows how to breathe as one body.

Guide speaks one last time into the old dark over the new wood.

GUIDE:

You built farther than grief alone could carry.

Chug rests one hand on the table.

CHUG:

Yeah.

GUIDE:

Good.

You'll need more than that where Four and below begin.

Chug does not ask what exactly that means.

Not tonight.

He just looks at the names that remain.

Ree.

Friend.

And everything beyond them.

Then he says the sentence camp has earned.

CHUG:

We're ready enough to keep going.

SYSTEM:

"CAMP STRUCTURE LEVEL: COMMAND HUB"

"ALLY KAIS — FULL ACTIVE"

"ALLY M.R. — TABLE SEAT ESTABLISHED"

"NEXT ACT VECTORS: REE / FRIEND / LOWER RANKS"

[BOSS GATE — Nexter No.3 Veyr]
The route compresses. Everyone feels the rank pressure before the strike.
This is the wall for THE SECOND TABLE.

41.text:
[SCENE 1 — THE TWO NAMES LEFT]
Only two unrecovered names remain on the board.

REE.
FRIEND.

The camp feels that.
Not as sorrow.
As unfinished structure.

Harjeev runs a fingertip under both names before the morning report.

HARJEEV:
Two names left on recovery.
Which means from now on every mistake is either impatience or stupidity.
Try not to invent new categories.

Kais is upside down on a watchbeam for no reason anyone sane can justify.

KAIS:
I can invent at least three.

O.O:
No.

KAIS:
I wasn't asking permission.

Yassine leans on the second table and studies Ree's line.

YASSINE:
What do we know?

Neon answers first because signal work made him closest to fragments.

NEONKD:
Ree kept rhythm teams moving.
Close support.
Impact discipline.
Not a sniper.
Not a sprinter.
Somewhere in between.
The kind that makes other fighters feel faster than they are.

Solo folds his arms.

SOLO:
And if they took that skill,
they didn't use it for pursuit.
They'd use it for control cadence.
Silence rooms.
Stop-start fields.
Break timing.

Knight places a black shard on the board.

KNIGHT:
Five.
Sable Vorn.

The room stills.

ADDY:
Silence fields.

SORYA:
Not just silence.
Selective muting.
A field that kills command,
kills rhythm,
kills rescue timing,
kills warning before impact.

M.R stands one pace off the table,
still bandaged,
still thinner than he should be,
still somehow shaping the room simply by refusing to lean on pain.

M.R:
If Five is holding Ree,
then he isn't guarding a prisoner.
He's guarding a metronome.

Chug hears that and knows it is right before anyone confirms it.

CHUG:
Then we go before Five teaches the camp how to lose its own timing.

[SCENE 2 — THE MARKET OF DEAD BELLS]
The route goes west into a place Harjeev calls Bell Market
and Knight calls Silence Market
because the bells hanging there haven't rung in years.

The difference between those names matters.

Bell Market is memory.

Silence Market is doctrine.

They go light on paper and heavy in truth.
Chug.
Yassine.
Addy.
O.O.
Knight.
M.R.
Kais.
No large camp move.
No convoy.
No obvious rescue shape.

Harjeev hates letting M.R out of the med line.

HARJEEV:
If your side opens on my route,
I will personally recover you just to complain while sewing.

M.R:
That threat is losing freshness.

HARJEEV:
Good.
Then survive long enough for me to repeat it.

Kais grins at M.R as they walk.

KAIS:
You know,
being medically forbidden and strategically necessary is one of the most attractive things a man can be.

M.R doesn't even look at him.

M.R:
That says more about your standards than my condition.

KAIS:
Exactly.
That is why we would make terrible life decisions together.

O.O:
If you keep saying things like that,
I'm going to start assuming concussion.

The road to Silence Market is all hanging frames and bell towers with their tongues removed.
Every gust tries to ring them.
Nothing answers.
The place feels mutilated.

M.R stops at the first gate and looks up at the gutted bronze.

M.R:
He likes symbolism.

KNIGHT:
You know Sable.

M.R:
I know the type.

That is not an answer.
Chug hears the gap.
Stores it.

Not now.
Later.

[SCENE 3 — THE FIRST FIELD]
The first silence field feels wrong before it feels empty.

Chug opens his mouth to warn left
and no sound comes.

Nothing.

Not muffled.
Not swallowed.
Denied.

Addy's curse makes no sound either.
Kais's grin sharpens,
because even he understands what that means.
Only Sorya's earlier lessons make sense of the room.

Selective muting.

Knight's hand signs cut the panic before it grows.
Two fingers down.
Left palm open.
Rotate.

They move.
Good.

Then the first strike lands.
Not on flesh.
On certainty.

A hidden challenger unit comes from the hanging bell frames with padded shoes and blunt sound-killing clubs.
No war cry.
No warning.
No audible footwork.

O.O is first.
Of course.

She catches one by the wrist and drives a reverse blade into the collar seam with such clean economy that the silence somehow feels louder around it.

Addy climbs a broken tower without command.
Good.
M.R doesn't fight full-speed,
but he points once,
sharp,
and Chug follows the line to the right bell chain where three more muted fighters are using the hanging metal as cover.

Frame-bolt.
One down.

Yassine and Kais take the lower seam.
Kais can't joke because the field won't let him.
He suffers in visible silence.
Yassine almost laughs mid-kill and then remembers he can't.

The field dies only when Knight reaches the hidden anchor—an iron tongue nailed into the base of the market well—and tears it free.

Sound returns all at once.

KAIS:
I hated every second of that.

O.O:
Good.

KAIS:
No, I mean spiritually.
I'm not built for quiet.
It's violent.

M.R:
That was the point.

[SCENE 4 — REE'S MARK]
At the center well they find a rhythm score carved into the stone lip.
Not music.
Combat count.

Three short.
One hold.
Two break.
Repeat.

Neon would have read it fastest.
He's not here.
So Addy does.

ADDY:
Ree's work.
He always counted impacts like someone teaching his body not to waste anger.

Yassine touches the carved count.
Then pulls his hand back.

YASSINE:
I know this.
I don't know from where.
But I know it.

M.R's eyes flick toward him.
That same unreadable warmth.
That same terrible self-control.

M.R:
Good.
Follow the count.
Five will have buried the honest path under silent paths.
Ree would mark the one that still remembers cadence.

Knight watches M.R once.
Really watches.
Then nods.

KNIGHT:
Take the count.

They do.

Three short corridors.
One held turn.
Two breaks through dead shutters.

At the end of that pattern waits Sable Vorn's chamber.

[SCENE 5 — SABLE VORN]
Five sits beneath the dead bells like a priest of mutilated language.

Not massive.
Not weak.
Beautiful in the way knives sometimes are.

Long black coat over layered field plates.
One hand holding a tuning rod of dark iron.
The other resting on the shoulder of a seated figure whose wrists are bound to two bell posts.

Ree.

Alive.
Head bowed.
One ear bled dry at the edge.
One glove wrapped around a strike baton still clutched too tightly to be fully unconscious.

Sable smiles when they enter.

SABLE VORN:
Good.
Enough of you came to make the room meaningful.

Chug steps forward.

CHUG:
Let him go.

Sable taps the tuning rod once against the floor.

The whole chamber falls silent.

No ambient sound.
No cloth rustle.
No foot scrape.
Only the ugly inner sense of blood moving in ears.

REE lifts his head slowly.

His lips form a word.
No sound.

M.R reads it anyway.

M.R:
He says don't rush.

Sable turns.
Interested.

SABLE VORN:
So you kept that.

Again.
An enemy saying it knows him.
Again.

Chug feels that and hates it.
Not now.
Focus.

Knight's fingers sign the whole room into war.

[SCENE 6 — END OF 41]
The first exchange happens in absolute silence.

Addy versus high bell chains.
O.O versus field guards.
Yassine and Kais breaking side anchors.
Knight taking Sable's center line.
Chug driving for Ree's binds.
M.R standing just outside full fight pace,
reading the chamber,
pointing the truths.

He points once at Chug.

Left bell.
Not Ree.

Chug obeys.
Breaks the left bell support instead of the prisoner line.
The whole field wavers.

Good.

Sable notices.
Smiles with less amusement.

SABLE VORN:
There.
A real room after all.

The cut to black is not visual.
It is auditory.

The entire chamber becomes a war no one can call by voice.

42.text:
[SCENE 1 — FIGHT IN MUTED AIR]
Sable Vorn's chamber kills command.
So the camp fights on preparation.

Knight's hand signs.
Addy's tower lane.
O.O's kill pace.
Yassine's break rhythm.
Kais's impossible noise made visual through spinning steel and light instead of sound.
Chug's direct acceleration.
M.R's pointing.

Ree sees all of it through half-lidded eyes.
His head still bowed.
But the old discipline in him watches count and spacing even under restraint.

Sable is elegant in the worst way.
Every time he moves the tuning rod,
one layer of sound returns somewhere else and dies here.
He doesn't just silence.
He redistributes what people rely on.

YASSINE almost steps wrong under that.
Kais catches him with a disc snapping across the floor in front of the boot.

Too close.

Yassine nods once in thanks.
Kais answers with a theatrical salute no one can hear.

O.O kills the first anchor guard.
Addy destroys the second bell brace.
Knight keeps Sable from resetting center.
Chug reaches Ree's post.

The bindings are not chain.
They're vibration locks.
Brute force will clamp them tighter.

M.R sees it from across the room and shapes the answer with hands only.
Three.
Hold.
Two.

Ree's count.

Chug breathes to it.
Three strikes along the post seam.
One held pause.
Two frame-bolts into the locking tongues.

The restraint opens.

Ree falls forward.
Still gripping the baton.

Alive.

[SCENE 2 — REE WAKES MOVING]
Ree does not wake like Yassine did.
Or Addy.
Or Solo.

He wakes mid-fight.

The first thing he does is catch the baton properly.
The second is stand on the same count Chug just used to free him.
The third is hit a silent guard across the jaw with such disciplined force that the man's feet leave the floor.

Good.

Very good.

Sable actually steps back.

SABLE VORN:
There.
That is why I kept you breathing.

Ree's first audible word only arrives because Addy shatters the last high bell and sound returns in fragments.

REE:
...Camp?

It comes out raw.
Broken by field stress.
Still enough.

CHUG:
Yeah.

REE looks at him.
Then at M.R.
Then at the room.
Everything old and new colliding at once.

REE:
You all got uglier.

KAIS, delighted:
Oh.
He's perfect.

[SCENE 3 — FIVE'S LAST ROOM]
Now the chamber truly turns.

Sound returns.
Sable hates that.
Good.

Kais becomes unbearable in the best possible way the second his voice comes back.

KAIS:
Did you miss me, you elegant corpse?

SABLE:
No.

KAIS:
Liar.
Everyone misses me by the third sentence.

O.O:
Stop helping him hate us in different ways.

Sable redraws the field around remaining bells and tries to cut command again.
Too late.
Camp rhythm has him now.

Ree shakes the numbness from his left hand,
rolls the baton once,
and steps into the pattern like he'd only been away a week instead of whatever hell transfer time did to him.

ADDY:
Can you move?

REE:
Can you shoot?

ADDY:
Yes.

REE:
Then I can move.

That is enough.

Sable doesn't lose to one fighter.
He loses to rhythm restored.

Addy takes his sight lines.
O.O takes his nearest kill angles.
Yassine ruins his field anchors.
Kais puts ringing steel into every dead silence he tries to rebuild.
Knight denies him center.
M.R calls the true count.
Chug and Ree hit on it.

One.
Two.
Hold.
Three.
Break.

The final break is Ree's.
Baton across the tuning rod wrist.
Crack.
Chug's frame under the sternum seam.
Knight's blade at the throat.
O.O's reverse grip at the kidney line.
Addy's arrow above the eye.

Sable goes still.
Not because fear taught him.
Because the room finally stopped belonging to him.

SABLE VORN:
...Quiet.
At last.

REE:
No.
You just lost the count.

Chug tears the Five insignia free.

[SCENE 4 — FIVE FALLS]
Sable withdraws badly.
Bleeding at wrist and center seam.
The bells around him all split as he moves.
Good.
Let him leave with silence broken behind him.

He does not beg.
Good.
Drakos don't.
He does not promise revenge either.
Better.
That means the defeat was cleaner than ego.

SABLE VORN:
Four will fortify what I could not mute.

KNIGHT:
Then Four can learn the same lesson.

Sable's eyes flick once toward M.R.

SABLE VORN:
If he is still with you by then.

That line lands.

Too hard.
Too deliberately.

M.R does not react where anyone can see.
Which is a reaction all its own.

Sable leaves.
Five down.

[SCENE 5 — REE IN CAMP]
Back at camp,
Harjeev inspects Ree the way he inspects everyone:
like sentiment is a waste until pulse proves itself.

HARJEEV:
Pupils acceptable.
Hearing damaged but not lost.
Coordination irritatingly intact.
Good.
Sit.

REE:
You got more unpleasant.

HARJEEV:
You got rescued late.
Both things happen.

Neon sees Ree and actually loses words for one whole breath.

NEONKD:
...
Ree.

REE:
Still ugly, Neon.

NEONKD:
Yeah.
Good.
You too.

That is the reunion.
Harsh.
Perfect.
True.

Yassine watches it and something in his face loosens.
A little.
Enough to matter.

M.R remains at the edge of the room.
Ree looks toward him longer than toward most.
Then says nothing.
That matters too.

Harjeev updates the ledger.

DRAKO NO.5 —
SABLE VORN
DEFEATED

Then:

REE —
ACTIVE / RECOVERY FAST
SILENCE DAMAGE —
MANAGEABLE
FIELD RHYTHM IMPROVED

Ree grips the baton across both palms and looks at the table like he already understands camp function without needing orientation.

REE:
Who's left?

Chug answers because he has to hear the truth from his own mouth.

CHUG:
Friend.
Then the lower ranks.

Kais leans back and whistles.

KAIS:
Well.
That means the fun gets catastrophic.

O.O:
Your idea of fun concerns me.

KAIS:
Good.
Keeps chemistry alive.

43.text:
[SCENE 1 — ONLY ONE NAME LEFT]
Friend is the last unrecovered name on the board.

That makes the room strange.

The others are here now.
Not whole.
Not perfect.
Present.

Friend remains absence with a title too intimate for war.

Harjeev says it out loud while morning dust still floats over the second table.

HARJEEV:
One name left before lower-rank campaign closes.
That makes this next move emotionally stupid by default.
Correct yourselves before I have to.

Solo rests the chain-sickle against the bench.

SOLO:
He wasn't weak.

Chug looks at him.

SOLO:
Friend.
He wasn't weak.
Don't let the name fool you.

O.O folds her arms.

O.O:
Names never fool me.
People do.

Neon slides a signal shard across the table.
A fortress icon.
Square nested in square.
Nothing graceful in it.

KNIGHT:
Four.
Tyrvak.
Fortress discipline.

M.R:
He won't bait with emotion first.
He'll build a structure around Friend and force us to exhaust ourselves against correctness.

REE taps his baton twice on the table edge.

REE:
Then we don't hit the fortress.
We hit what teaches it to close.

Knight's eyes flick toward him.
Then nod once.

KNIGHT:
Good.

Ree shrugs like approval costs nothing.
It does.
That is why he makes it look cheap.

[SCENE 2 — WHAT FRIEND MEANS]
The road to Tyrvak's ground begins through abandoned checkpoints and wall fragments.
Every tenth stone is still standing.
Every eleventh is not.
Tyrvak doctrine all over it.
A man who values sequence enough to punish irregular numbers.

Kais walks backward for three straight minutes just to annoy the geometry.

KAIS:
If Four likes order,
he's going to have a terrible time with me.

O.O:
You are not strategy.
You are interference.

KAIS:
The best kind.

Addy walks beside Chug this time,
bow slung,
fully active now,
fully part of field assignments.

ADDY:
What was he like?

CHUG:
Who?

ADDY:
Friend.
Don't make me say the obvious things for you.

Chug takes a while.

CHUG:
He was...
the one who held people together before any of us knew that was a job.
He remembered birthdays.
Water counts.
Arguments.
Who needed pushing.
Who needed shutting up.
Who needed to be left alone for one hour instead of one week.
Stuff nobody ranked until it was gone.

Yassine hears that and goes quiet.

M.R hears it too.
Looks away toward the road.

That matters.
Again.

[SCENE 3 — THE FORTRESS THAT WALKS]
Tyrvak's field isn't a castle.
It's worse.

A moving fortress.
Modular wall sledges locked into square formations over old rail lines.
Shield crews.
Pike lanes.
Arrow slits.
Rotating bastions.
Everything capable of advancing while pretending to stand still.

And at its center,
visible through three layers of defensive geometry
stands Friend.

Upright.
Bound into the command mast by metal straps and field wires.
Not caged like a prisoner.
Mounted like a stolen standard.

That makes every person from camp angry in a slightly different way.

KAIS:
That is deeply rude.

O.O:
I will cut him apart for that alone.

KNIGHT:
No.
You'll cut the formation apart.
The man can wait.
The geometry cannot.

Friend lifts his head slowly.
Sees them.
Does not smile.

FRIEND:
Took your time.

Chug nearly laughs at the cruelty of how familiar that sounds.

CHUG:
Yeah.
Getting tired of hearing that.

FRIEND:
Then move faster.

Even strapped to a mast,
he sounds like himself.

Good.
That helps.
And hurts.

[SCENE 4 — TYRVAK]
Tyrvak emerges only when the camp comes into full view of the formation line.

He walks on top of his own moving fortress like command made flesh.

Huge shield.
Not defensive.
Directive.
Everything about the armor says line holder,
discipline anchor,
punishment for improvisation.

TYRVAK:
So the camp came in person.

Knight steps forward once.

KNIGHT:
Release the bound man.

TYRVAK:
No.
He is useful.
He understands cohesion.
I wanted to see how your camp behaves watching its own spine made into architecture.

M.R speaks before Chug does.

M.R:
You built a wall around the wrong idea.

Tyrvak's gaze shifts.
Locks.

TYRVAK:
And yet I still prefer your original to your current arrangement.

That line lands harder than Tyrvak's shield would.
Because of who he says it to.
Because of what it implies.
Because Chug hears it and cannot not hear it.

Not now.
Field first.
Always field first.

[SCENE 5 — FORTRESS BATTLE]
Tyrvak's war is the opposite of chaos.

That makes it infuriating.

Every enemy unit holds.
Every line closes.
Every retreat becomes another wall.
Every successful strike from camp finds itself paying for three disciplined answers.

Knight splits the camp into stacked cells to answer.
Addy and Neon on high-signal angle.
O.O and Ree on mast approach.
Solo and Yassine on wheel-cut and undercarriage.
Kais creating interference across the rail seams.
Chug center breach.
M.R and Harjeev running table logic from the field relay stone.

Yes.
They brought the board concept with them.
Good.
Camp is faction now.

Tyrvak sees it.
Hates it.
Good.

CHUG hits the first shield train.
Doesn't break through.
Of course.
Tyrvak designed this to consume frontal pride.

REE:
Not center!
Hit the locks!

Chug adjusts instantly.
Better than old Chug.
Good.

O.O reaches the second mast ring and cuts three wire couplings before the fortress rotates a wall panel between her and Friend.

Addy arrows the slit hinges.
Neon cracks the relay timing with signal flares off polished plates.
Kais runs his discs along the rail teeth and literally derails one support cart because he is that kind of nightmare.

KAIS:
There.
Now it's art.

SOLO:
You are genuinely sick.

KAIS:
Yes.
Still useful.

[SCENE 6 — FRIEND'S VOICE]
The formation grinds forward even while losing pieces.

Friend watches the whole thing with a terrible calm.

FRIEND:
You're stronger.

CHUG:
Yeah.

FRIEND:
Still messy.

CHUG:
Also yeah.

FRIEND:
Good.
That means you lived.

That line hits almost everybody.

Friend isn't just a name.
He really was the one who held the soft tissue between them.

Tyrvak notices the emotional drag.
He presses harder.
Shield slam.
Pike wheel.
Advance.

TYRVAK:
Cohesion is property.
You lost him.
I improved him.

That earns the first truly ugly look Chug has ever seen from Addy.

ADDY:
No you didn't.

Good.
Anger is aligned.
Useful anger.

[SCENE 7 — END OF 43]
By the time dusk bleeds over the rail smoke,
camp has damaged the moving fortress but not stopped it.

Friend is still bound.
Tyrvak is still behind walls.
The field is not lost.
Not won either.

Knight pulls the retreat correctly.
Because this is Four's lesson:
if you do not own the structure yet,
do not die trying to flatter yourself.

Chug hates retreating.
Does it anyway.

At the fallback ridge,
Friend's voice carries once through the steel and smoke.

FRIEND:
Come back smarter.

Kais adjusts his hat and looks at the broken rail.

KAIS:
Well.
I hate respectable enemies.
Makes killing them feel like paperwork.

44.text:
[SCENE 1 — THE NIGHT OF PLANS]
No one sleeps properly.

Tyrvak did exactly what Four should do.
He made the camp retreat without losing identity.
That makes him dangerous enough to respect.
And therefore harder to kill.
Respect always complicates clean violence.

The second table becomes a war engine through the night.
Knight draws structure layers.
Neon maps relay timing.
Addy rebuilds the angle charts.
Ree sets cadence marks for team rotations.
O.O marks hidden blade entry points on the fortress sketch.
Solo calculates chain capture loads.
Kais throws discs at pegs until his pattern shows which rail teeth are decorative and which are load-bearing.
Harjeev counts what can be spent.
M.R watches.
Then begins changing everything.

Not because Knight was wrong.
Because M.R sees the part still built like a challenge instead of a collapse.

M.R:
You're still trying to defeat Tyrvak.
Defeat the fortress instead.
The man follows.

Knight studies the board.
Long.
Then steps back.

KNIGHT:
Show it.

That is trust.
Or necessity.
Often they look identical.

M.R moves the markers.
Not fast.
Not dramatic.
Accurate.

M.R:
Addy and Neon don't attack kill lines.
They blind command windows.
O.O doesn't climb the mast.
She kills the wheel-men.
Solo uses chain-sickle to lock shield wagons into each other.
Ree runs cadence shock through the undercarriage posts.
Kais turns the rail release into a false collapse on the east side.
Chug doesn't breach front.
He enters through the rescue cavity after the command mast loses balance.

Yassine watches the whole thing carefully.

YASSINE:
You talk like you've broken one before.

M.R doesn't answer immediately.

Then:

M.R:
I've watched enough walls die.

Again.
An answer that is one layer too thin.
Again.
Not tonight.

[SCENE 2 — FRIEND'S CAVITY]
They return at first iron-light.

The moving fortress is already rolling.
Of course it is.
Tyrvak wastes nothing.
Not even dawn.

This time the camp attacks as one system.

Neon blinds the command slits with bouncing signal flares.
Addy threads impossible shots through momentary gaps created by those flashes.
O.O kills the wheel-men silently one after another.
Solo's chain-sickle binds two shield sledges together so the formation turns against itself.
Kais breaks the east rail teeth in a pattern that suggests structural failure where there is only tactical collapse.
Ree runs the strike count loud enough for camp to move on it.
Yassine cuts any recovery team that thinks the old angles still exist.

Tyrvak sees the pattern too late.

TYRVAK:
...There.

Not praise.
Recognition.

Good.
They have become enough to force it.

Chug doesn't hit the wall.
He waits.
Hates waiting.
Does it anyway.
Then the rescue cavity opens exactly where M.R said it would.

CHUG:
Now!

He goes through.

Not alone.
Yassine with him.
Because camp doesn't rescue through singular pride anymore.

They hit the inner mast.
Friend's bind rig is not decorative.
It's structural.
Tyrvak really did mount him into cohesion.

Chug starts to cut.
Friend barks once:

FRIEND:
Not that side!
Load line!

Yassine changes angle immediately.
Blade to the load line.
Ree's cadence echoes from outside.
Three.
Hold.
Two.
Break.

The mast lurches.

Friend tears one arm free himself and grabs Chug by the collar hard enough to hurt.

FRIEND:
You really did get slower.

CHUG almost laughs.
Almost.

[SCENE 3 — TYRVAK FALLS]
Once Friend is no longer part of the wall,
the wall becomes killable.

That is the whole lesson.
Always was.

Tyrvak realizes it at the same moment camp does.
He abandons command height and drops into the center lane with shield first.
Massive.
Disciplined.
Furious in the most controlled way possible.

He almost reaches Friend.
That was his real target all along.
Keep the spine mounted.
Keep the camp watching itself displaced.

No.

O.O intercepts at the knee.
Solo hooks the shield edge.
Kais turns the stagger into drift by clipping the boot plate with a spinning return.
Addy and Neon blind the visor slit with two impossible lines at once.
Ree's cadence forces the whole camp into the same strike beat.
Yassine cuts the shield strap.
Chug opens Rage 1 clean and drives the frame straight through the exposed chest seam beneath the lifted shield arm.

Tyrvak drops.

Flat.
Like a fortress section finally realizing gravity is not a negotiation.

TYRVAK:
...Good.

Friend,
still half-strapped and bleeding,
looks down at him with no softness at all.

FRIEND:
No.
Just overdue.

That line belongs on the table.

Chug takes the Four mark from Tyrvak's armor.

TYRVAK doesn't ask for mercy.
Doesn't offer threat.
He only says:

TYRVAK:
Three breaks command itself.
Don't let your camp admire its own shape too much.

Then he withdraws in disciplined ruin,
dragging a shattered shield that no longer knows how to be a wall.

[SCENE 4 — FRIEND RETURNS]
Back at camp,
Friend refuses the cot.

Harjeev wins that argument in under six seconds.

HARJEEV:
Sit or I write you down as hostile architecture.

Friend sits.

Good.

He looks older than the others expected.
Not by years.
By held things.
The kind of old that comes from carrying the mood of a room too long.

Yassine studies him.

YASSINE:
Do I know you?

Friend looks at him and all the sharpness softens into something ugly with care.

FRIEND:
Yeah.

YASSINE:
Good.
Another one.

FRIEND:
Sorry.

YASSINE:
No.
It's fine.
I think.

Friend looks to Chug next.
Then to M.R.
That moment lasts one breath too long.

FRIEND:
So.
We're all here now.

M.R answers first.
Quietly.

M.R:
Almost.

Friend hears the word under the word.
Almost who.
Almost what.
Almost whole.

He doesn't push.
That matters too.

[SCENE 5 — END OF 44]
Harjeev updates the board.

DRAKO NO.4 —
TYRVAK
DEFEATED

Then:

FRIEND —
ACTIVE / RECOVERY STABLE

The roster side of the table now looks impossibly full.
Too full for the early camp.
Exactly full enough for war.

Kais leans over the board and whistles.

KAIS:
Look at that.
Someone could fall in love with this.

O.O:
No.

KAIS:
Counterpoint,
yes.
